engagements.title: Feature Request
engagements.body:
I'd like the ability to "dial in" the triggers a bit further.  For 
instance, the text we need to use right now for an email that triggers 
when an order is complete is something like this:

"If the attached invoice has not been paid, it is due prior to shipping 
or pickup. "

and this:

"If your order is shipping, you'll receive tracking information once it 
ships."

I'd like a better filter in the trigger, so that the text I send them is 
more clear, and more specific information personalized to their 
situation.
To do this, I would need to be able to filter the following:
order status is set to complete and the order has been paid for.Shipping 
Method is set to Freightquote.comShipping method is set to UPSShipping 
method is set to customer pickuporder status is set to complete and the 
order has not been paid for.Shipping Method is set to 
Freightquote.comShipping method is set to UPSShipping method is set to 
customer pickup
Then create 6 different triggers, instead of 1 generic one.

engagements.body: This is the first year renewal for Lane 17 Cabinet, Co. proceed to prepare data and engage the customer to execute a renewal meeting.

02/11/25 Retention Plan Meeting Context: Alex asked when his contract is up and I confirmed with him it will end as of March 10th. He wants to keep his data for 90 days so he can come back and potentially get back into Allmoxy. The goal of this meeting is to determine a gameplan with Alex to see what will be needed for him to start using the system in 90 days and also confirming that his access will be removed during the 90 days. Agenda: Pause timeframe - looking for 90 days Do you feel that you'll have bandwidth in 90 days? Anticipating more time available? What's left to complete within the catalog? How can we hit the ground running once the 90 days are up? Removing payment method as of March 10th (loose access after that) Scheduling a time to re-sync after 2 months of pause to see how bandwidth is looking and if we can plan to resume the project. Notes: Meeting recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/view/Lane-17-Allmoxy-Quick-Sync::01JKR8NYAZ435KQC9MSDPE0CNA Takeaways: Alex hasn't had the bandwidth to invest into setting up Allmoxy as he needs it to function. Alex learned throughout the last year that he and his partner, Jason, need to first define their catalog offering within Microvellum so they can then use this outline to match up Allmoxy. Essentially they put the horse in front of the cart and weren't ready to actually implement Allmoxy. New plan I've removed their payment method from their account so once the next charge date hits they won't be charged. I'll be reaching out to Alex in mid May to see how the backlog of work is coming along and if anticipates having the bandwidth to dive back into Allmoxy. Confirming with product how long the data will be stored if someone hasn't logged in or submitted a payment (believe this is 12 months)

Check-in Meeting (Catalog progress) 10/3/24 Agenda: Catalog progress How has the work been going? Any issues? Platform familiarity Feeling more comfortable since you've been building the catalog? What's next? Our services team is waiting on information to build out the door only product lines, correct? What's your timeline look like for being able to start using the system? Next Steps Share the information with me and I can get it to Juan/Aaron Schedule a touch base call for the end of the month Notes: Still has multiple projects on his plate. Door only products - could use sooner rather than later Get clarity from Juan - what information is needed for the doors.

When a customer calls us for thermal foiled products, we typically need the following:

1) Door Style

We also provide other thermal foil products.

1) 1/4 - 3/4 panels flat press 1 side all edges (1.5 inches wide by 96 inches long is the smallest)

2) 1/4 - 3/4 panels 2 sided no edges

3) 1/4 - 3/4 panels custom shapes and sizes

4) 1/4 - 3/4 panels full wrap (closest back, white, black, color matched?)

Currently we would like to offer:

1) 15-20 door styles

2) Ability to request a custom door style

3) Edge Profile default choice (1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 3/8)

4) Ability to add as many doors/panels as necessary

5) Ability to customize edge profile on any door (so default edge when door style is chosen, but can change edge on any door necessary and it overrides default)

6) Ability to change color/texture on a per door/panel basis.

7) Thermal foil color/texture automatically changes sqft pricing appropriately. (ie. solid colors are cheaper than gloss etc.)

engagements.title: Next Steps: Palmetto Wood Doors — 2026-07-01
engagements.body:
- Renewal date (June 18) already passed with no action -- check billing/subscription status now.
- Re-engage Andy directly: they never confirmed launch after months of pricing validation work in late 2025.
- Clean up duplicate renewal deal cards for this account (same automation issue seen elsewhere).

Onboarding Status Stalled mid-onboarding, and the renewal date already passed without resolution. Deal closed-won June 2025 ($385/mo). Extensive implementation work happened June-Oct 2025 (pricing formulas by wood type/labor, Cabinet Vision integration, Stripe setup) -- none of which is reflected in HubSpot notes (only the original sales demo is logged there). Went quiet after Oct 22, 2025, still in pricing validation with no confirmed launch. The company's renewal deal closedate (June 18, 2026) already passed 13 days ago with no action -- and, matching a pattern seen elsewhere, 3 duplicate "Renewal" deal cards were auto-created since March 2026. Last Touchpoint October 22, 2025 -- Call -- Carson Ward & Ray Cantu with Andy Ryals -- Building a master door product with customizable pricing (materials/labor by wood type), still explicitly in validation phase ("Andy emphasized the importance of validating the pricing system with real orders"). No contact found since. Last Action Item Owner: Customer (Andy). Was to send real order examples with door-by-door pricing to validate the system. No evidence this was received or followed up on --8+ months of silence since. Use Case & Launch Readiness Palmetto Cabinet Doors (Andy Ryals, NC door manufacturer, ~$500k/year, 75 doors/day) wanted to move off manual text-message ordering and Cabinet Vision manual entry onto Allmoxy for online ordering, instant pricing, and cut-list/invoice automation. Extensive pricing configuration work was done but launch was never confirmed -- they appear to have been paying for a system they hadn't started using in production. Sources Checked HubSpot (3 notes total -- essentially just the original demo; the entire implementation effort is NOT reflected in HubSpot notes), Fireflies (7 additional calls found June-Oct 2025 showing real onboarding progress), Gmail/Jira not separately checked given time. Flag: Renewal date already passed (June 18, 2026) with no resolution, on an account that may never have launched. Recommend checking billing/renewal status urgently alongside a direct customer check-in.

engagements.body: Spoke with Bud and let him know that he can continue building his catalog while the pause is in place. He was very excited and appreciative of this.

Pause Request 9/30/24 Bud reached out saying that their sales have dropped throughout August and September which lead to his leadership asking his team to cut all unnecessary expenditures. He'd prefer to have a temporary pause (3 months) so they don't lose the work he's completed so far and that they can move forward with leveraging Allmoxy. At this time it seems to be an expense they can't afford. Bud's original email: "So, company sales took a downturn in August. Everyone thought that we would see a rebound in September. Well, that has not happened yet, and management is a bit anxious. I have been asked to suspend any expenditures that I possible can at this point in time.We need to pause or terminate our Allmoxy account as soon as possible. Of course I would rather suspend the account and let it be dormmate until such time that we could reactivate. Hopefully, that will be the first of year. I’m assured that the Allmoxy format is seen as a viable part of the business going forward, but now is a time for immediate cutbacks. The option of complete termination is something that I and the management team do not want to pursue. The likelihood of the company starting from scratch in the future is not likely to happen. Can you reach out to the powers that be at Allmoxy and respond to this email with a course of action that we both can abide by. The suspension of billings needs to be immediate. As in end of business today. If you can make that happen the team at Wedgewood will be very grateful. Please reach out with any questions regarding this request." I've responded to Bud by including Mekenzi and Broc so they can help determine an appropriate plan of action with hopes we can get them reactivated at the beginning of the year as Bud mentioned. @Broc Hill @Mekenzi Falslev for vis.

engagements.body: Churn Risk Playbook Please share the most up to date health pulse from the CSM's perspective. Red(this customer is not in good standing and is on track to churn) Has this customer asked to pause or cancel their account or is this playbook being utilized preemptively? Requested to cancel Notes: They requested to pause for 2 months until March because they "didn't have time for Allmoxy right now". They seemed like they were coming back and eager to get started again. Now they are booked out for the entire year and are unsure if Allmoxy fits into the big picture of the recent changes they have made. "Yes, we are booked for most of the year and won't have time to implement it. In addition, we aren't sure how it will even integrate with our current business model. We have a lot of other major changes going on currently, and want to focus on those." How much is the customers monthly subscription? Please note if the customer has received any reductions in MRR during their lifetime with Allmoxy as well as any significant, recent implementation costs. $250.00 Industry Segment (Data Confirmation) Custom Cabinet Shop Business Size (Data Confirmation) SMB How long have they been a customer of Allmoxy? 04/15/2025 Is this customer launched? No Is this customer working with our implementation team now, if so please elaborate on the nature of the work/project. No Is this customer a legacy/strategic account? No Has the customer proposed any solutions that would eliminate or delay their churn risk? This could be a price reduction or delivery on a specific feature. Notes: No, they are already paying our lowest price. They are just too busy to keep going. Please share any other strategic context that we should consider related to this account. (Ex. Industry influence/connections, personality details, known expansion opportunity, competitor tech stack, etc.) Notes: This customer had a rough start to implementation. They expected Aaron to tell them how to price and had no pricing method prepared. When asked how they currently priced their products, they didn't really know. They got frustrated about the export process, and thought that Aaron should be the Mozaik experts and not them. They didn't really understand their own software. But then things started to get much better implementation-wise. We were going strong for a few weeks, and then they just kept pushing meetings back because they got too busy. If they had clear documentation to start the process, I think we could have cut implementation time down by a month. Who's the main customer contact associated with this escalation? Ezra For reporting purposes, please check that this playbook is completed. Yes

Onboarding meeting #2 with Ezra and Michael (10/13/25) Review Stripe Connected? Triggers (enable Ezra and Michael to receive emails or texts for tasks) Review triggers Hiding categories to only show to verified customers? For testing, make sure to have a test account with a verified customer trigger. Today Price adjustments Financial settings Shipping Meeting Summary Josh and Michael discussed several key configuration areas within Allmoxy, focusing on tax setup, shipping preferences, financial workflows, and price adjustment mechanisms. The goal was to tailor Allmoxy for both B2B and consumer workflows, ensuring flexible payment handling, controlled shipping access, and pricing customization for various customer types. Key Takeaways Ezra’s Initial Questions Ezra created a test account but noticed sales tax wasn’t being calculated. It was later confirmed the system was correctly applying the 6% tax. Discussion arose around how Allmoxy handles tax-exempt customers. Michael mentioned Cornish had never charged sales tax and was exploring how to handle tax going forward. Josh clarified Allmoxy uses TaxJar for sales tax calculations, updating automatically based on customer or company zip codes unless a custom tax rate is applied. Shipping Michael asked how to restrict shipping for homeowners and require local pickup. Solution: Use tags (e.g., “homeowner”) to control which customers see specific shipping methods. Created a “Will Call” method only visible to users with the “homeowner” tag. Businesses can see both “Will Call” and standard delivery. Custom shipping formulas were implemented: <10 miles = $75 10–20 miles = $150 >20 miles = $250 Josh used ChatGPT to generate and test formulas for local delivery pricing. FedEx/UPS shipping integration is available but relies solely on weight, not dimensions. Price is returned from the carrier, and a multiplier (e.g., x2.3) is applied to estimate final charge. Recommendation: test average order weights to balance profitability and fairness. Financial Settings Allmoxy defaults to a “pay first” model, like Amazon. Michael expressed preference to offer limited credit to known local companies and default to prepayment for unknown or consumer customers. Options discussed: Use credit limits (e.g., $2,000) and build limits (e.g., $5,000) per company. Set defaults for all new customers and override for trusted accounts. Create tags like “local” or “verified” to govern payment terms. Trigger notifications for overdue payments and include terms in automated messages (e.g., full payment due before shipment). Payment methods: Stripe integration is used. It stores cards securely and allows repeat billing. ACH payments have lower fees. Stripe processing fees (~2.9%) can be offset with hidden price adjustments if needed. Invoices & QuickBooks: QuickBooks Online integration is in beta. In the meantime, use CSV export and third-party tools (e.g., Transaction Pro) to import Allmoxy data into QuickBooks. Manual journal entry is also a viable option for now. Price Adjustments Allmoxy supports automatic surcharges and discounts on a per-line-item basis. Adjustments can be: Global (e.g., 10% discount for all orders), Tag-based (e.g., surcharge for all “homeowner” accounts), Product-specific (e.g., MDF doors only), Company-specific (e.g., a discount for a trusted cabinet shop). Priority settings determine which adjustments apply if multiple are active. Suggestion: clean up inactive or unused price adjustments to reduce confusion. Price adjustments are not shown to customers if intended to offset fees (e.g., Stripe). Action Items Michael to review and confirm tax strategy with his new accountants, especially concerning tax exemption and resale scenarios. Create additional shipping methods as needed, tied to customer tags. Test and finalize the local delivery formula using known addresses. Set up default credit and build limits, and tag-based rules for verified vs. non-verified customers. Determine initial Stripe surcharge offset approach (e.g., via hidden price adjustment). Clean up old or inactive price adjustments in the system. Consider simple rules and low credit limits for new/unknown customers to mitigate risk. Monitor QuickBooks integration progress or explore third-party import tools in the meantime. Next Steps Internally align on credit policy for new vs. existing customers (e.g., default limits, pay-first tagging). Finalize shipping and delivery strategy for homeowner vs. business customers. Build task automation and triggers for overdue payments, order status, and onboarding. Revisit 3D Designer in January once deprecated, and assess new consumer-facing tools Allmoxy may release (e.g., Cabinet Portal). Gather Mosaic or Cabinet Vision files if participating in the developer raffle for file testing.

Onboarding meeting #1 with Ezra & Michael Triggers Trigger for Mosaic manual review will notify the internal team when products with a specific tag (e.g., “Mosaic Manual Check”) are included in an order. This is to flag attributes that cannot be imported directly into Mosaic. New company creation trigger will send an email alert to designated employees (e.g., Ezra and Michael) when a new company signs up. Verified order trigger will notify the customer when an order has been verified and can also send internal users an export file to drop into Mosaic. Welcome email trigger can be sent automatically upon account creation to outline next steps and expectations (e.g., “Please allow 24 hours for account verification”). A proposed trigger will automatically apply a “non-verified” tag to new companies, restricting their access until approved. Tags Product tags: Used to group products requiring special handling or triggering (e.g., for Mosaic manual imports). Company tags: "Verified Customer": Grants access to full catalog and standard pricing. "Non-Verified Customer": Default for all new accounts; limits access until reviewed. "Homeowner" and "Business": Used to segment product/category visibility. Category and product visibility can be controlled using the "company exclusive" setting with tags. Some products (e.g., MDF doors) may need to be duplicated to allow tailored visibility for homeowners vs. business customers. Tags can be used to apply different price adjustments based on customer type. Company Creation Customers will be allowed to create their own accounts rather than requiring manual setup. Upon signup, a company will: Be required to submit their EIN (configured as a custom field). Automatically receive a “non-verified” tag. Be hidden from all product categories unless verified. Admins will receive a notification via trigger upon each new company signup. Admins must manually review the company and change the tag from “non-verified” to “verified customer” if approved. Contact Creation Each company must have at least one associated contact. Admins can create individual contact profiles for employees or customers. Internal employees (e.g., shop staff) can be added with customized permission levels. Customers created manually must have “make payments” permission explicitly enabled. Login credentials (username and temporary password) can be created manually when adding a contact. Internal users can test contact permissions by logging into accounts directly using assigned credentials. Custom Fields A custom field for EIN Number was added to the company signup form. Field Name: EIN Number Variable Name: ein_number Set as required for new business account creation Field is editable and visible during sign-up Additional custom fields can be added as needed for internal qualification or filtering. Custom field responses will populate directly into the company’s contact page. Meeting Summary The team met with Josh Baker from Allmoxy to walk through account configuration, Mosaic export setup, product visibility management, and automation via tags and triggers. Key features were demonstrated and tested, including restricting catalog access for unverified customers, sending automated emails, and configuring shipping methods and Stripe payments. The goal was to finalize backend logic and begin internal testing of customer workflows and pricing configurations. Key Takeaways Important Discussions Product attributes were updated for MDF doors, slab doors, floating shelves, and applied panels. Mosaic exports are functioning for most product types; MDF and slab door exports still need testing. Tags and triggers will be used to manage visibility, approvals, and Mosaic import limitations. Front-end and pricing logic will be finalized before customer onboarding. Orders will be verified internally before being locked from customer edits and moved into production. Technical Issues & Fixes Applied panel pricing formulas were not saving properly; Aaron resolved this during the call. Audio issues at the beginning of the meeting were resolved by switching devices. Bid deletion process was clarified and demonstrated. Decisions Made Self-service account creation will be allowed but controlled using verification workflows. EIN will be required at signup to help distinguish businesses from homeowners. Verified customer tag will unlock full catalog visibility; non-verified customers will see no products. Stripe will be the payment processor; setup will begin soon. Products may be duplicated for different customer types where necessary. Challenges or Concerns Visibility setup using tags and duplication can become complex and needs careful testing. Search bar visibility for restricted products cannot currently be disabled. Stripe requires detailed company information and may delay payment processing if not set up early. Action Items Ezra to: Complete testing of Mosaic exports for MDF and slab doors. Set up and test product visibility rules using dummy accounts and tags. Finalize trigger for Mosaic import alert. Review and configure Stripe payment processing. Set up welcome email and new company alert triggers. Josh to: Send Allmoxy knowledge base/articles to Ezra. Assist with trigger and pricing formula setup as needed. Michael to: Align with Ezra on customer approval workflows and pricing structure. Review Stripe onboarding requirements. Next Steps Begin internal testing using dummy accounts with homeowner and business tag combinations. Finalize Stripe integration and run test transactions. Configure and test customer visibility, order flow, and trigger emails. Duplicate products and assign tag restrictions where needed for specific customer types. Continue exploring triggers, pricing adjustments, and process automation in next week’s session. Next follow-up meeting scheduled for Thursday with a focus on trigger implementation and potential launch preparation.

Call with Ezra 9/3/25 Getting frustrated with the implementation process. They feel like they gave us a lot to do last week and we only delivered on part of it They wanted a few other products in there (slab doors, drawer boxes, MDF doors, and Floating Shelves) All we did was the floating shelves. Highlights how we are currently having a bandwidth issue on the implementation team. The information was in the ticket- I just don't think Aaron had time to get to the rest of it New customers in implementation should be getting more priority than launched customers with project work Meeting Summary The meeting centered around the status of floating shelf product setup within the catalog, including product structure, validators, pricing, and development communication. The team discussed ongoing issues with incomplete implementation, lack of expected deliverables, and the need for a more efficient workflow between the client and the development team. Key Takeaways Important Discussions The floating shelf category was initially imported from another catalog but will now be recreated in-house to match the desired look. A new category for Floating Shelves should include sub-products: Floating Shelf Left, Floating Shelf Right, and Floating Shelf Wall-to-Wall. The current product setup includes only four shelf products, which are incomplete — missing pricing, images, validators, and mock-up data. Technical Issues & Fixes No pricing is being generated for the floating shelf products in the system. Validators to restrict invalid dimensions are missing: Maximum width should be restricted to 96 inches. Minimum thickness should be 2 inches (to avoid users inputting 1.5" thickness, which is unbuildable). Expectations were that the system would automatically apply markups and differentiate floating shelf pricing from cabinet boxes, but this is not happening. Box material product attribute was created, but the floating shelf markup column hasn't been fully implemented. Decisions Made The team will mimic the look of the originally imported shelf product but rebuild it within the internal catalog. Josh will meet with Aaron during the next scheduled session to: Review last week’s progress. Clarify what was expected and what was actually completed. Align on the list of deliverables. Josh requested a clear specification document from the client outlining attributes, pricing, and rules for each product (e.g., drawer boxes, slab doors, floating shelves). Challenges or Concerns The client expressed concern over the slow progress and lack of deliverables despite being billed hourly. Frustration was shared about having to attend development meetings without technical value-add, while still being charged. Client feels the communication loop is broken — lack of clarity on what is needed from them and delayed responses are stalling progress. Client reiterated a desire for offline development based on clear specs, rather than real-time collaboration during meetings. Action Items Josh & Aaron to review: The work done last week. The original meeting recording for specifications (especially for drawer boxes and slab doors). Client to resend the Google Drive with project documents (already sent to Josh B. at Allmoxy). Aaron to: Implement pricing logic and markup for floating shelves. Add necessary validators (width and thickness). Ensure product images and mock-ups are in place. Team to clarify what deliverables were expected vs. completed for transparency and billing alignment. Client offered to provide additional clarification by phone if needed during development — emphasized preference for being consulted rather than delayed due to uncertainty. Next Steps Josh to meet with Aaron during the next session to align expectations and confirm what was completed. Team to prioritize completing floating shelves with: Pricing, Validators, Correct product structure and mock-ups. Client to remain available for real-time clarifications as needed — preferred over waiting for weekly meetings. Further products like drawer boxes, MDF doors, and slab doors to be implemented once specifications are confirmed and last week’s scope is completed. Continued communication to ensure development progresses offline with minimal disruption to the client’s time.

Canary & Allmoxy Sales Training Meeting Canary & Allmoxy Sales Training Meeting December 19, 2025 11:15 AM MST 25 mins sarah@allmoxy.com madison@allmoxy.com sales@canarycc.com ap@canarycc.com View Meeting Recording Customer Account Management and Tagging The team clarified the structured approach to customer account creation and tagging to ensure correct pricing and product visibility. Sarah Pierce outlined the account hierarchy where a company acts as an umbrella for multiple contacts, each requiring login access to Almoxy, with individual homeowner and retail customer accounts as alternatives (03:02) Contacts must be linked to their company to enable login and permission controls. Tags are critical for product availability and pricing, with Tony and Michelle responsible for tag management. Correct tagging ensures contractors and dealers see accurate pricing tiers and product selections. This tagging system directly supports differentiated customer experiences and revenue management. Financial settings were explained, including two checkout flows: pay before processing and credit limit, with recommended credit limits for new customers set between $5,000 and $10,000 (06:27) Pay before processing requires payment before orders reach ordered status, controlling cash flow upfront. Credit limit allows orders up to a set limit before payment, keeping the order pipeline active without upfront payments. Order limits typically exceed credit limits to permit multiple pending orders before payment clears. Grace periods and finance charges are configured to enforce timely payments and manage receivables risk. Order Entry and Folder Organization Order entry processes were optimized for speed and clarity using order-level settings and folder structures to improve client experience and internal handling. Sarah introduced order-level settings that allow global attribute changes (like closet color) across all products in an order, reducing manual updates for customers and sales reps (12:41) Customers can apply changes globally or selectively to new products, streamlining order edits. Folder-level settings extend this control to subsets of products, helping differentiate sections within larger orders. This feature supports faster quote revisions and customization, enhancing client satisfaction. Sarah planned to send supporting articles for further training on these features. Folders act as an organizational tool to divide large orders by space or project segments, such as separating closets or kitchen components, with subtotaling at the folder level improving bid clarity (15:19) Folders enable clients to view and manage the order in manageable segments, improving transparency. Sarah noted potential production implications as folders may split similar product lines, which needs confirmation from Tony to avoid disrupting cut lists. The team agreed the client-side clarity outweighs potential production complexities, pending testing. The folder feature was identified as a solution to client confusion with long, undifferentiated parts lists. Reporting and Sales Visibility The discussion highlighted report usage for sales tracking and commission attribution, emphasizing the need for accurate tagging and order status management. Sarah emphasized that sales reports depend on orders reaching the “status to charge customer,” which varies by client and can affect report reliability (20:19) Some customers are charged at different order statuses, causing timing discrepancies in sales data. Orders report allows filtering by entered date and tags, enabling sales reps to track their orders and commission-related activity. Tagging customers or orders with sales reps’ identifiers is essential for accurate commission tracking and sales attribution. Product tagging can also track push efforts on specific items by filtering orders containing those products. Invoice reports provide comprehensive financial visibility including credit card fees and finance charges, supporting broader accounting and revenue management needs (22:50) Sales focus remains primarily on orders and sales reports, with less emphasis on aging and collections reports for the sales team. The reporting capabilities support performance monitoring and strategic sales efforts. Integration and Workflow Alignment The team confirmed current workflow integration between design and order systems, supporting smooth data transfer and order management. The team confirmed Tony and Michelle handle exports from Closet Pro to Almoxy and export order data as needed for Excel and other reports (23:50) This integrated workflow supports seamless transition from design to order entry without redundant data entry. Exported data supports downstream operational needs such as production planning and financial reconciliation. Continued coordination between sales, design, and operations teams is implied to maintain data accuracy and efficiency. The process supports scalability and reduces errors in order processing. Training and Knowledge Transfer The meeting focused on foundational training for new team members to ensure consistent use of Almoxy and enable effective sales operations. Sarah and Madison committed to sending detailed articles covering folders, order-level settings, company creation, and contact creation to support Melissa’s onboarding (24:20) This training material aims to unify workflows and reduce inconsistent practices across the team. Melissa’s intention to blend different user approaches into an optimized personal workflow was acknowledged as positive. Ongoing support remains accessible through Madison for clarification and advanced questions. The materials and follow-up will improve onboarding speed and operational consistency. Action Items Sarah Pierce Send training articles on folders, order-level settings, company creation, and contact creation to Melissa for further review. (24:20) Melissa Discuss folder usage and potential production impact with Tony to ensure it does not disrupt production workflow. (18:10) Communicate with Tony and Michelle regarding tagging structure and financial settings to confirm accuracy and consistency. engagements.body: Called Chesky to see if he meant to decline the scope call with Juan and Sarah and he said yes that he wanted to reschedule. He is going out on Holiday but wants Kenzi to call back on the 28th and get something on the calendar.

Retention Meeting October 2024 In attendance: Broc, Kenzi, Chesky Chesky has fallen off the wagon for months with attempting engagements and has been unresponsive. He was very disgruntled in the spring and we turned off his payment.  In the spring he said that he wanted to continue to try to make Allmoxy work and Kenzi reached out several times without him showing up. He randomly booked the retention meeting without reaching out providing the purpose behind the meeting. Goal: to understand where the partnership would be valuable moving forward, create an action plan that makes sense. Chesky is trying not to have customers enter all parts through Allmoxy because they get frustrated. The shop benefits from it but for customers it is a pain the neck. When you have a couple thousand parts to enter it's very time consuming. The way that Allmoxy prices things is very good, you can have a base price, a square footage price but the part he is looking for is the backend office materials, etc. and it comes down to price and what it will cost and take time wise to get setup and see if it's worth it. Essentially wanting a scope for next steps to see where it would take them and what it would look like. Chesky mentioned that he wanted to see how other closet manufacturing shops utilize Allmoxy. Broc feels like there are a lot of variables when it comes to that. And he is unable to show others who are using it. But when he can say is that there are other closet shops that use it for parts and kits (more of a sku'd product) and things like he does and does it successfully. But Chesky does custom closets. They are either having clients do either one of two things. Either having their clients create the order on the front end, or they're allowing almoxy to take client data through an import CSV file and upload it into almoxy. He currently exports out of closet pro and into closet vision. It isn't completely accurate. When they import into closet vision they are able to see it pretty well and tweak it to what it needs to be. Whereas with Allmoxy all he sees is parts. He doesn't know where and what to tweak and it get's confusing. Sarah and Juan would be the best people to ask what solutions there are as they are in thick of it with our customers and can better speak to what that looks like. Without Allmoxy what are the alternatives in your mind? Chesky said build something from scratch but he doesn't want to do that. We don't want them to do that either. What do you see the value of Allmoxy being for dollar wise? The deal we gave him was $899 a month. Our base price is $1099. If Allmoxy is not the main software he isn't sure if he wants to pursue it or not. He is getting in a lot of orders. Inventory, purchasing, etc. are a pain point from him. He wants to make it as simple as possible. What Chesky needs: To understand what is the best way for customers to come into closet pro without customers going through 800 parts. Second, see how much time and money it would take to build the back end of the office functionality side of things such as inventory and pricing etc. We should be able to get this back to him beginning of next week. He could get on Monday or Tuesday. Broc is scheduling a scope call. Chesky said if he doesn't hop on to please call him and remind him to hop on. The catalog isn't laid out super well right now. The way closet pro is laid out is in sections not by parts. Chesky showed us a demo of closet pro/cabinet vision and what it looks like and said he would be willing to show a demo of what it looks like on the scoping call to help us better understand the full picture. Next steps: Get on a no cost scope call with services team with Sarah and Juan since Sarah understands the closet side of things very very well. Broc booked a time for Chesky and team next week. Broc/Kenzi will follow up with Chesky after the scope call to create an action plan moving forward. Fireflies recording: To see what Chesky shared regarding CV and Closet Pro please go to minute 18:21 to view the demo. https://app.fireflies.ai/view/Allmoxy-CS-Sales-Retention-Meeting-uniplank-com::Wk6AZlCNV4itf76f

8/7/26 - B2B PO Output Troubleshooting - https://app.fireflies.ai/view/Wurth-LAC-Allmoxy-Multiple-Vendor-POs::01KZCH69J3MK78H4VP7YBYYZ52 Agenda: Screen recording of Mary's PO issues. Meeting Summary Carson (Allmoxy) and Mary Hartley (Wurth LAC) met to walk through Wurth's order/PO process ahead of integrating Slide-A-Shelf as a new customer Goal was to confirm that Slide-A-Shelf orders can generate the correct separated documentation for multiple vendors (Wurth Lac, Lewis, Quality Craft) Mary walked through her existing workflow on the Wurth site: bids, verification, PO entry, and pulling invoices from QualityCraft's supplier portal Overall process is a close match to what Allmoxy already supports; no major issues surfaced Key Takeaways Important Discussions Mary demonstrated the full order lifecycle: customer places a bid, order is verified, PO is entered in SAP, and drop-ship orders route to the correct supplier (e.g., QualityCraft) through Wurth's B2B portal Freight must be quoted correctly in Slide-A-Shelf's system based on parts, since Wurth's shipping fee pulls from the customer's connected FedEx account Every order is treated as an individual order and gets its own PO; Wurth cannot batch multiple orders under a single PO Customers occasionally combine products from different vendors (e.g., adding drawers to a door order) even though this is discouraged, since it creates conflicting POs and billing across separate vendor systems Mary noted this cross-vendor combination has only happened about twice and does not anticipate it being a frequent issue for Slide-A-Shelf Carson referenced an earlier conversation with Jamie indicating that Wurth's service team proactively calls customers who order more than six products, which should reduce the likelihood of large multi-vendor batch orders Carson and Mary reviewed a sample Wurth product page together (searching for the correct "Worth LAC" company/product listing) to confirm product setup, options, and the measuring guide acknowledgment checkbox Carson noted Wurth may eventually want to simplify or remove the measuring guide acknowledgment step, as it can feel lengthy to customers, though Wurth uses it to ensure customers understand fit requirements before ordering Mary confirmed all billing for Slide-A-Shelf orders will run through Wurth, meaning end customers will not be able to pay directly on the Wurth/QualityCraft side Technical Issues & Fixes No new technical issues were identified during the walkthrough; Mary's SAP experienced a brief slowdown during the demo but this was not treated as a system issue Decisions Made Carson will update the Slide-A-Shelf invoice page so it matches the same field structure/layout as the QualityCraft invoice (including PO number field) Carson will retain the existing separate-order/separate-PO structure rather than building a batching mechanism, since combined vendor orders are rare Challenges or Concerns Risk of customers combining products from different vendors (e.g., doors and drawers) into a single order, which causes PO and billing mismatches across separate vendor systems Ensuring Slide-A-Shelf correctly quotes freight based on parts so it matches Wurth's connected FedEx shipping calculation Action Items Carson: Update the Slide-A-Shelf invoice page to match the same field structure as the QualityCraft invoice Carson: Create a test order on the Slide-A-Shelf site under the Wurth LAC company, select one product, and send the order link to Mary for review Mary: Review the test order Carson sends to confirm the PO number and invoice details are correct Next Steps Carson will confirm with Jamie before formally creating the test order Wurth may consider revisiting the measuring guide acknowledgment step in the future to reduce friction for customers, though no commitment was made on this

engagements.title: Wurth LAC: Track Slide-A-Shelf B2B go-live
engagements.body: Per the 6/10/26 meeting, Slide-A-Shelf products are built but marked unavailable pending markup from Jeremy Mitchell and Carson's system config. Confirm the markup is finalized, products are toggled live and Chris and Mary are onboarded. Keep launch momentum. Source: note 6/10/26.

6/10/26 - Wurth and Slide-A-Shelf Meeting - https://app.fireflies.ai/view/Slide-A-Shelf-Wurth-LAC-Allmoxy-B2B-Meeting::01KT07QD6PTM5VE5K1F2VAQW6M Agenda: Both parties to determine markup and make products available Are we doing any price adjustment? (surcharge of any kind) Turn products to available Discuss next steps of Wurth's current internal processing of B2B orders to align with Slide-a-shelf's operations. Notes: Chris Godinez - joined since Mary couldn't make it due to family issues. Meeting Summary B2B partnership call between Slide-A-Shelf, Wurth LAC, and Allmoxy to align on pricing strategy, order processing workflows, system configuration, and pre-launch requirements Slide-A-Shelf products are built and integrated into Wurth's Allmoxy platform but are currently marked unavailable pending final pricing and markup decisions Meeting covered the full order lifecycle from customer placement through Wurth verification, PO entry, and Slide-A-Shelf production Leadership approval from Wurth's CEO and directors identified as a required step before the partnership goes live System configuration tasks assigned to Carson Ward, with follow-up items distributed across Slide-A-Shelf and Wurth teams Key Takeaways Important Discussions Slide-A-Shelf offers custom pullout shelves as direct-ship products through Wurth's platform, targeting cabinet makers and contractors who prefer not to build their own Wurth will use Allmoxy as the ordering and PO management platform; customers place orders through Wurth, Wurth verifies and enters POs, and Slide-A-Shelf downloads confirmed orders for production Slide-A-Shelf's 30-year brand history and product quality cited as key competitive advantages over brands such as Rev-A-Shelf New side-mount product includes rear sockets as an upgrade; an undermount version is in development and expected to launch first through Wurth Expansion opportunity identified: Slide-A-Shelf products could be promoted to cabinet manufacturers such as Lewis Cabinet Specialties and Timberline Cabinets, though all orders must flow through Wurth's system Orders for Slide-A-Shelf products mixed with other vendors must be split; customers should be directed to place separate orders per vendor to avoid fulfillment issues Technical Issues and Fixes Slide-A-Shelf products are currently visible internally to Wurth's team only and must be toggled to live after markup is finalized Carson confirmed the system supports a flat fee or percentage surcharge applied uniformly across all Slide-A-Shelf products as a placeholder markup Granular per-product pricing adjustments are possible but a standard markup is preferred as the starting point Email notification triggers can be configured to alert Wurth's team when a Slide-A-Shelf product order is placed, enabling order monitoring and split management Chris requested different status bubble colors for verified orders; Carson will investigate expanding color options Carson will set up Chris Codinez and Mary as contacts in the Wurth Slide-A-Shelf Allmoxy account for order verification and PO entry access Shipping charges and product costs are currently combined on invoices; separating them for accounting clarity is under discussion; Carson confirmed system flexibility to support either format Decisions Made Wurth customers will pay shipping separately at checkout; pricing strategy must account for freight costs to remain competitive Jamie Brinker will send Wurth wholesale costs, suggested retail prices, MAP pricing, and shipping cost details; Jeremy Mitchell's pricing manager will use this data to finalize the markup percentage Carson will implement the agreed markup in Wurth's Allmoxy system once confirmed Orders requiring measurement confirmation for six or more shelves will include a phone follow-up from Slide-A-Shelf to reduce costly errors All order price or measurement adjustments must be documented via email approval to maintain invoicing integrity A Slide-A-Shelf-branded letter, installation instructions, and hardware documentation will be included in shipments to Wurth customers; Worth branding adjustments are under review A dedicated support line for Wurth's Slide-A-Shelf customers has been established Carson will maintain a single email thread with all participants to centralize communication Challenges or Concerns Pricing must be set carefully to avoid Wurth's site listing products above Slide-A-Shelf's own retail pricing, which could cause customers to bypass Wurth Shipping costs are a complicating factor; unlike large retailers offering free shipping, Wurth customers will pay freight, which affects perceived competitiveness High product variability (over 15,000 variations) and custom measurement requirements create order accuracy risk; phone verification for larger orders is a current mitigation Brand naming on Wurth's platform requires care to avoid alienating other customers who may sell competing products Final approval from Wurth's CEO and directors is required before going live; Jeremy Mitchell will coordinate this review after pricing and documentation are finalized Action Items Jamie Brinker: Provide Wurth with Slide-A-Shelf wholesale costs, suggested retail prices, MAP pricing, and shipping cost details Jamie Brinker: Share the current thank-you letter draft and installation instructions with Wurth for potential branding adjustments Jamie Brinker: Coordinate internally to manage order adjustments with proper email approvals for price or measurement changes Jamie Brinker: Follow up with Stephanie and the accounting team regarding possible invoice format changes to separate shipping from product costs for Wurth Jeremy Mitchell: Determine the appropriate markup or surcharge to apply on Slide-A-Shelf products in Wurth's system, then communicate pricing strategy and margins to Slide-A-Shelf and the internal pricing team Jeremy Mitchell: Coordinate with CEO and directors for final review and approval of pricing, packaging, and partnership details before going live Jeremy Mitchell: Obtain and share Quality Craft paperwork with the Slide-A-Shelf and Wurth teams to ensure consistent documentation Chris Codinez: Collaborate with Jamie and Carson to finalize paperwork and PO processes, verify orders on Allmoxy, and add POs accordingly Chris Codinez: Provide examples of invoices and packing slips used with current vendors to Slide-A-Shelf for review and replication Chris Codinez: Test and confirm Allmoxy site access and order processing capabilities for Wurth Slide-A-Shelf users Carson Ward: Implement pricing adjustment setup on Wurth's Allmoxy system for Slide-A-Shelf products with ability to apply a uniform surcharge or discount, keeping open the option for granular adjustments if needed Carson Ward: Configure system triggers and notifications to alert Wurth's team of orders containing Slide-A-Shelf products and order status changes Carson Ward: Assist Wurth team contacts (Chris and Mary) with Allmoxy access setup for order verification and purchase order entry Carson Ward: Follow up with Chris and Mary on documentation workflows and integrate required paperwork automation in Allmoxy Carson Ward: Distribute meeting recording and summary notes to all participants and maintain a shared communication thread for updates Next Steps Pricing markup percentage to be confirmed by Jeremy Mitchell's pricing manager after receiving cost data from Jamie Brinker; Carson to implement in Allmoxy once confirmed Wurth products to be toggled live in Allmoxy after markup is finalized and system configuration is complete Paperwork and documentation formats to be aligned between Wurth, Slide-A-Shelf, and Quality Craft to replicate current vendor workflows Order notification triggers to be configured and tested in Allmoxy Wurth contacts (Chris Codinez and Mary) to be onboarded with Allmoxy access in the coming days Jeremy Mitchell to present full pricing, packaging, and partnership details to Wurth's CEO and directors for final approval prior to launch Marketing collateral and customer communication materials (literature, QR code cards, branded inserts) to be prepared by Slide-A-Shelf for inclusion in shipments following leadership approval Additional calls to be scheduled as needed to resolve outstanding questions before go-live

engagements.body: Rugby & Allmoxy | B2B Connection

12/11/25 - Onboarding Meeting (Meet with Evolve) https://app.fireflies.ai/view/FW-Allmoxy-Evolve-Cabinet::01KC2EF6N2XAJYWZ7A04G5QGSH Meeting Summary The meeting centered around the integration and setup of Stanley's custom door products within the Allmoxy platform for Rugby to resell. Discussions covered remaining technical issues, product setup steps, pricing configuration, materials management, and shipping logistics. A phased rollout strategy was proposed, including a plan to finalize configurations before the end of the year, with potential go-live in early 2025. Key Takeaways Important Discussions Stanley is waiting for Allmoxy to resolve a pricing issue related to panel thickness before proceeding with catalog sharing. The issue centers on mispricing the quarter-inch center door panel as a three-quarter-inch panel, affecting cost accuracy. A new material line (Tafisa from Rugby) will be added, but only once current pricing issues are resolved. Stanley clarified that Rugby customers should only see materials Rugby stocks, to avoid unsupported orders (e.g., Wilson Art in some markets). Custom product setup for Rugby’s instance will be handled through cloned versions of Stanley’s existing products, with limited material selections shown. Discussion around controlling the user experience: avoiding overwhelming material dropdowns and maintaining clean product presentation. Technical Issues & Fixes Current technical problem: Allmoxy misprices quarter-inch door panels as three-quarter-inch. Solution: Either document changes to send to Aaron for implementation, or set up a direct meeting with Aaron for a collaborative adjustment session. Future product flexibility depends on setting up accurate material depth attributes (e.g., panel thickness) and logic to avoid material bloat in user selections. Custom shipping weight (dim weight) must be manually input due to system limitations. Decisions Made Stanley will hold off on adding Rugby materials until the panel pricing fix is completed. Stanley will enable products for B2B resale once pricing is accurate, and Rugby will then pull them into their instance. Products for Rugby will be cloned and limited to Rugby-approved materials only. A single universal price adjustment will be used for all B2B products (instead of multiple per product). Future customer-specific attributes will be enabled when available to eliminate the need for cloned products. Local delivery will be handled by Rugby for nearby customers, and out-of-region freight will be managed directly by Stanley. Challenges or Concerns Risk of Rugby customers selecting unavailable or unreleased materials (e.g., Tafisa color not in the U.S.). Laminating veneer to match stock colors for quarter-inch panels is unreliable due to color variation. Teams issues on Stanley's end prevented screen sharing for product configuration during the meeting. Shipping complexity due to lack of integrated freight calculation (dim weight must be added manually). Action Items Stanley to: Finalize pricing corrections in Allmoxy for quarter-inch vs. three-quarter-inch panels. Provide list of products to be cloned and prepared for Rugby’s instance. Await Brandon’s list of stocked Tafisa SKUs (both quarter-inch and three-quarter-inch). Work with Carson to schedule a meeting with Aaron next week for pricing logic finalization. Brandon Anderson to: Send list of Tafisa materials stocked at Rugby. Carson Ward to: Coordinate the engineering meeting with Aaron and Stanley. Guide Stanley through enabling B2B product sharing via Allmoxy. Support configuration of cloned products with limited attributes for Rugby. Josh & Rugby Team to: Prepare for eventual integration of Allmoxy instance into the Rugby website (iframe or direct link). Test the ordering process once Stanley's catalog is ready. Next Steps Carson to send Aaron’s availability for a pricing review and configuration session with Stanley. Stanley to complete product setup and confirm pricing accuracy before cloning Rugby-specific versions. Rugby team to test ordering through Stanley’s instance once products and pricing are finalized. Determine shipping strategy per region: local via Rugby; freight handled by Stanley with manual input. Evaluate if temporary direct-link access can be used instead of iframe for faster Rugby launch. Target: Internal testing by January 1, 2025; public launch potentially by March 1, 2025.

Title: Allmoxy Kick Off Call Date: Tue Dec 09 2025 15:15:00 GMT-0500 (Eastern Standard Time) Participants: bobby@allmoxy.com, carson@allmoxy.com, jsilpe@rugbyabp.com Transcript: See full transcript Audio: Listen to audio Duration: 45 mins Overview - Integration with Evolve: Plans for a B2B iframe integration; no native products will be built initially. - Account Creation Control: Customers won't create accounts; access managed internally for pricing and catalog visibility. - Shipping Strategy: Local delivery for nearby customers; drop shipping from Evolve for distant deliveries. - Pricing Management: Pricing controlled internally to avoid exposure to errors; new customer accounts trigger notifications for verification. - Payment Processing: Payments handled through external ERP; merchant gateway on Almoxy will be disabled for financial transactions. - Next Steps: Meeting with Stanley on Thursday to finalize product setup, account management, and pricing permissions. Notes 👋 Introduction and Greetings Participants expressed excitement for collaboration and confirmed partnership with Evolve for B2B product selling. 👤 Role Introduction Carson Ward introduced as customer success/account rep responsible for guiding the connection with Evolve and deploying Almoxy for product integration and customer support. 🔄 Product Integration Focus No native product builds planned; focus on embedding Almoxy via iframe into Rugby’s site for seamless customer ordering directly from Evolve product catalogs. 🛠️ User Setup Demonstration Demonstration of adding users/contacts with permission settings in Almoxy system, highlighting how Brandon, Daryl, and Josh can manage accounts efficiently. 📅 Upcoming Call Preparation Scheduling and preparation for upcoming call with Stanley on Thursday to confirm product catalog availability and account setup essential before deep integration; Carson offered to join to facilitate communication. 🔍 Customer Account Creation Discussion Clarification that new customers creating their own accounts is possible but may not be ideal; discussion on price visibility control and setting proper pricing tiers via tags and account verification to avoid pricing errors or confusion. 📦 Order and Shipping Details Explanation that all order and shipping details flow through Almoxy/Evolve but that pricing and approvals are managed internally to maintain control. ⚙️ Account Setup Confirmation Identified that Rugby does not currently have an Evolve Almoxy account; setup and product readiness need confirmation from Stanley before catalog import. 🏷️ Tagging Mechanism Importance Tags introduced as a critical mechanism to control product visibility, pricing tiers, and customer segmentation; explained the mechanics of tagging on company accounts and product level, highlighting their fragility if deleted. 🚚 Shipping Logistics Discussion Shipping logistics discussed, with options including local delivery by Rugby trucks versus drop shipping directly from Evolve. Default shipping settings and customer restrictions can be configured accordingly. 🔒 Customer Account Control Decision Decision made to disable customer self-account creation on the Almoxy site to ensure Rugby controls customer onboarding, pricing, and access; new accounts created internally, then customers are emailed login info to ensure proper setup. 🔑 Controlled User Access Workflow Workflow clarified that customers cannot see pricing or catalogs without proper account setup and login, fitting Rugby’s controlled user access model. 🔗 Future SSO Implementation Discussion on future plan to implement single sign-on (SSO) so customers logging into Rugby’s site can access Almoxy catalog seamlessly without re-login. ✅ Next Steps Confirmation Confirmation that Thursday’s meeting with Stanley is the critical next step for account and product setup, followed by further implementation of iframe and API integration; Carson requested to be invited to that call. 📄 API Documentation and Support API documentation access available; technical integration will be handled by Rugby’s right technical contact, with Almoxy support routing questions as necessary. 🔚 Meeting Wrap-Up Final wrap-up confirms plan to review product availability with Stanley on Thursday, set up accounts, and proceed with technical integration afterwards. Action Items Josh Silpe Coordinate with Stanley to confirm product availability and enable catalogs for B2B on Thursday call Ensure that customer accounts are created internally before granting access to Almoxy catalog to control pricing visibility and user permissions Work with technical team to explore iframe and API integration for seamless catalog access from Rugby’s site Include Carson Ward on the Thursday call with Stanley for technical and operational support Brandon Anderson Confirm if Rugby has an Almoxy account setup with Evolve and prepare for account creation if not Onboard customer accounts and coordinate pricing/permission assignments before they access Almoxy Support logistics decisions for shipping options and delivery methods Carson Ward Assist in user/contact setup demonstration and support with permissions configuration Join Thursday call with Stanley to facilitate product catalog enablement and account setup Disable customer self-account creation option on Almoxy site per Rugby’s security policy Provide training and guidance on tagging, financial settings, shipping configurations, and permissions management Share API documentation and assist in routing technical questions Send meeting recording and recap following call Stanley Enable and finalize product catalog and pricing for B2B access via Almoxy

Technical Issues & Fixes Current technical problem: Allmoxy misprices quarter-inch door panels as three-quarter-inch. Solution: Either document changes to send to Aaron for implementation, or set up a direct meeting with Aaron for a collaborative adjustment session. Future product flexibility depends on setting up accurate material depth attributes (e.g., panel thickness) and logic to avoid material bloat in user selections. Custom shipping weight (dim weight) must be manually input due to system limitations. Decisions Made Stanley will hold off on adding Rugby materials until the panel pricing fix is completed. Stanley will enable products for B2B resale once pricing is accurate, and Rugby will then pull them into their instance. Products for Rugby will be cloned and limited to Rugby-approved materials only. A single universal price adjustment will be used for all B2B products (instead of multiple per product). Future customer-specific attributes will be enabled when available to eliminate the need for cloned products. Local delivery will be handled by Rugby for nearby customers, and out-of-region freight will be managed directly by Stanley. Challenges or Concerns Risk of Rugby customers selecting unavailable or unreleased materials (e.g., Tafisa color not in the U.S.). Laminating veneer to match stock colors for quarter-inch panels is unreliable due to color variation. Teams issues on Stanley's end prevented screen sharing for product configuration during the meeting. Shipping complexity due to lack of integrated freight calculation (dim weight must be added manually). Action Items Stanley to: Finalize pricing corrections in Allmoxy for quarter-inch vs. three-quarter-inch panels. Provide list of products to be cloned and prepared for Rugby’s instance. Await Brandon’s list of stocked Tafisa SKUs (both quarter-inch and three-quarter-inch). Work with Carson to schedule a meeting with Aaron next week for pricing logic finalization. Brandon Anderson to: Send list of Tafisa materials stocked at Rugby. Carson Ward to: Coordinate the engineering meeting with Aaron and Stanley. Guide Stanley through enabling B2B product sharing via Allmoxy. Support configuration of cloned products with limited attributes for Rugby. Josh & Rugby Team to: Prepare for eventual integration of Allmoxy instance into the Rugby website (iframe or direct link). Test the ordering process once Stanley's catalog is ready. Next Steps Carson to send Aaron’s availability for a pricing review and configuration session with Stanley. Stanley to complete product setup and confirm pricing accuracy before cloning Rugby-specific versions. Rugby team to test ordering through Stanley’s instance once products and pricing are finalized. Determine shipping strategy per region: local via Rugby; freight handled by Stanley with manual input. Evaluate if temporary direct-link access can be used instead of iframe for faster Rugby launch. Target: Internal testing by January 1, 2025; public launch potentially by March 1, 2025.

Title: Allmoxy Kick Off Call Date: Tue Dec 09 2025 15:15:00 GMT-0500 (Eastern Standard Time) Participants: bobby@allmoxy.com, carson@allmoxy.com, jsilpe@rugbyabp.com Transcript: See full transcript Audio: Listen to audio Duration: 45 mins Overview - Integration with Evolve: Plans for a B2B iframe integration; no native products will be built initially. - Account Creation Control: Customers won't create accounts; access managed internally for pricing and catalog visibility. - Shipping Strategy: Local delivery for nearby customers; drop shipping from Evolve for distant deliveries. - Pricing Management: Pricing controlled internally to avoid exposure to errors; new customer accounts trigger notifications for verification. - Payment Processing: Payments handled through external ERP; merchant gateway on Almoxy will be disabled for financial transactions. - Next Steps: Meeting with Stanley on Thursday to finalize product setup, account management, and pricing permissions. Notes 👋 Introduction and Greetings Participants expressed excitement for collaboration and confirmed partnership with Evolve for B2B product selling. 👤 Role Introduction Carson Ward introduced as customer success/account rep responsible for guiding the connection with Evolve and deploying Almoxy for product integration and customer support. 🔄 Product Integration Focus No native product builds planned; focus on embedding Almoxy via iframe into Rugby’s site for seamless customer ordering directly from Evolve product catalogs. 🛠️ User Setup Demonstration Demonstration of adding users/contacts with permission settings in Almoxy system, highlighting how Brandon, Daryl, and Josh can manage accounts efficiently. 📅 Upcoming Call Preparation Scheduling and preparation for upcoming call with Stanley on Thursday to confirm product catalog availability and account setup essential before deep integration; Carson offered to join to facilitate communication. 🔍 Customer Account Creation Discussion Clarification that new customers creating their own accounts is possible but may not be ideal; discussion on price visibility control and setting proper pricing tiers via tags and account verification to avoid pricing errors or confusion. 📦 Order and Shipping Details Explanation that all order and shipping details flow through Almoxy/Evolve but that pricing and approvals are managed internally to maintain control. ⚙️ Account Setup Confirmation Identified that Rugby does not currently have an Evolve Almoxy account; setup and product readiness need confirmation from Stanley before catalog import. 🏷️ Tagging Mechanism Importance Tags introduced as a critical mechanism to control product visibility, pricing tiers, and customer segmentation; explained the mechanics of tagging on company accounts and product level, highlighting their fragility if deleted. 🚚 Shipping Logistics Discussion Shipping logistics discussed, with options including local delivery by Rugby trucks versus drop shipping directly from Evolve. Default shipping settings and customer restrictions can be configured accordingly. 🔒 Customer Account Control Decision Decision made to disable customer self-account creation on the Almoxy site to ensure Rugby controls customer onboarding, pricing, and access; new accounts created internally, then customers are emailed login info to ensure proper setup. 🔑 Controlled User Access Workflow Workflow clarified that customers cannot see pricing or catalogs without proper account setup and login, fitting Rugby’s controlled user access model. 🔗 Future SSO Implementation Discussion on future plan to implement single sign-on (SSO) so customers logging into Rugby’s site can access Almoxy catalog seamlessly without re-login. ✅ Next Steps Confirmation Confirmation that Thursday’s meeting with Stanley is the critical next step for account and product setup, followed by further implementation of iframe and API integration; Carson requested to be invited to that call. 📄 API Documentation and Support API documentation access available; technical integration will be handled by Rugby’s right technical contact, with Almoxy support routing questions as necessary. 🔚 Meeting Wrap-Up Final wrap-up confirms plan to review product availability with Stanley on Thursday, set up accounts, and proceed with technical integration afterwards. Notes 📋 Initial Context & Introduction Bobby Lewis conducting Allmoxy software demo from Vegas trade show for The Job Shop, a small cabinet shop in Hellertown, Pennsylvania. The Job Shop specializes in custom drawer boxes and received referral from Manhattan client doing $7.5 million in residential casework annually. Client requested they use Allmoxy for billing and payment processing for drawer box orders. The Job Shop targeting five major players in Manhattan market, with potential $500K annual drawer box spending per client. Company uses Mosaic CNC for cabinetry and Kantec dovetail machines for drawer boxes. 💻 Software Overview & Customer Portal Allmoxy creates branded customer portal at company.allmoxy.com with custom logos and optional custom domain. Customer self-service portal allows clients to place orders, see pricing, and track delivery dates Amazon-style. Integrated Stripe payment processing at 2.9% rate vs QuickBooks' 3.5% rate, saving 0.6% on credit card transactions. QuickBooks integration in beta for seamless transaction sync. System includes drawer box templates ready for implementation. Automated triggers send customer notifications for order confirmations, shipping updates, and completion notices. 📦 Inventory Management & Production Features Barcode scanning system for tracking products through production with printable labels for drawer boxes. Supply system tracks inventory automatically, allocating materials when orders verified and comparing against minimum quantities. Work schedule management organizes production by delivery dates with start/stop job tracking. System can generate packing slips, invoices, and shipping reports automatically. Tax Jar integration calculates appropriate tax rates by customer location. Bobby's previous experience: managed $1.6 million monthly production with one secretary using Allmoxy. 🚀 Advanced Features & Development Roadmap Project scheduling and Gantt chart functionality identified as 2025 development priority. Full API integration available with Zapier connectivity for third-party calendar and scheduling systems. System supports customer-specific pricing with granular discounts by company tags or individual products. Cabinet operation scaling available beyond drawer boxes for dealers wanting manufactured parts. Money collection improvement: Bobby's experience showed reduction from 62-day to 14-day average aging on 30-day terms. 💰 Pricing Structure & Implementation Timeline Monthly subscription model based on annual revenue processed through system, locked for 12 months then adjusted based on actual usage. Implementation cost: approximately $300-400 for 2 sessions with implementation engineer for drawer box setup. Customer success representative included in subscription for ongoing support. Setup timeline: estimated 2 hours for simple solid maple dovetail drawer box product configuration. Hybrid build approach recommended where client learns formula writing alongside implementation engineer. engagements.title: Next Steps: Subtle Cabinets — 2026-07-01
engagements.body:
- Make a final decision: unpaid since Dec 2025, internal question about removing access has sat unresolved since April. Close it out one way or the other.
- If reactivating: reach out to Marques/Evan directly, don't assume they've churned without asking.
- Clean up billing/access accordingly once decided.

Onboarding Status Stalled mid-onboarding AND unpaid since December 2025 -- likely a churn case that was never formally closed out. Kicked off April 2025, made real progress through May 2025 (pricing formulas, labor rates, meta attributes for casework/doors/drawers), then went quiet. Separately, payments stopped in December 2025. Last Touchpoint Direct implementation: May 14, 2025 -- Call -- Carson Ward & Aaron Dundas with Evan and Marques (Subtle Cabinets) -- Finalized detailed pricing formulas (casework, doors, drawer boxes) with next steps for Evan/Marques to self-serve data entry. Internal: as of April 15, 2026, Carson was still asking internally "these guys haven't paid since December, are they churned or do we need to remove access?" -- suggesting this was never resolved. Last Action Item Owner: Allmoxy (Carson/Madison). Per Jan 14, 2026 internal notes, Carson was to follow up on the failed payments and request an updated card; Madison was to monitor contract/escalation status. As of April 15, 2026 this was still an open question with no clear resolution, and nothing found since. Use Case & Launch Readiness Subtle Cabinets (Marques, Bay Area cabinet shop) wanted Allmoxy for pricing/catalog management integrated with Cabinet Vision. They made solid onboarding progress on pricing logic but appear to have never fully launched with live orders, and stopped paying in December 2025. This reads as a customer who quietly disengaged rather than one still working toward launch. Sources Checked HubSpot (6 notes, stop mid-May 2025, but includes the April 2026 internal flag about non-payment), Fireflies (8 additional internal meetings Jun 2025-Apr 2026 mentioning Subtle Cabinets only in the context of payment/contract escalation, never a resumed implementation call), Gmail/Jira not separately checked given the clear billing-driven story already found. Flag: This looks like an unresolved churn that's been sitting in limbo for ~7 months (unpaid since Dec 2025, internal question about removing access never actioned). Recommend a clear decision: formally close/reactivate, don't leave it open-ended.

5/14/25 - Catalog working session - https://app.fireflies.ai/view/Subtle-Cabinets-Allmoxy-Working-Session::01JV2Q35MHS1ZHRREB3P5BXYG7 Pricing information they shared as of 5/13 is attached. Agenda: Review pricing sheet provided Talk about materials and attribute selections Confirm where Evan and Marques need to enter data for pricing to start calculating. Meeting Summary The meeting involved Carson Ward, Evan, Marques B, and Aaron Dundas reviewing the pricing structure setup in Allmoxy. Evan is transitioning into the primary role of managing Allmoxy-related tasks, while Marques focuses on Cabinet Vision and CNC processes. The goal was to clarify the labor and material pricing logic within Allmoxy, validate current formulas, and empower Evan and Marques to configure and manage pricing independently. Key Takeaways Important Discussions Role Assignments: Evan will manage Allmoxy pricing and configuration going forward; Marques will handle Cabinet Vision and CNC-related tasks. Pricing Formula Structure: Labor and material pricing were discussed in depth, focusing on clarity, customization, and future flexibility. Casework pricing (base, tall, wall, vanity) is calculated using lineal footage multiplied by labor rates. Door pricing is based on square footage, with fallback minimums for small door sizes. Drawer box types (e.g., dovetail, rollout) have differentiated labor costs. Use of Allmoxy Meta Attributes: Meta attributes were introduced to assign custom labor rates based on cabinet type and product characteristics. These attributes allow scalable, global pricing changes and keep labor logic clean and consistent. Meta values must be manually added to each product and defaulted to appropriate values (e.g., “base”, “wall”). Material and Hardware Costing: Pricing tables can include hardware like Blum Tandem glides. Material pricing factors include square footage, waste percentage, and margin settings. Rollout and drawer box labor included separately from material. Technical Issues & Fixes Missing data in the shared pricing sheet (e.g., door per sheet data line) was clarified and corrected. Some final square footage calculations (e.g., for slab doors) didn’t save in the spreadsheet but were resolved in discussion. Proxy formulas were built and tested during the session for pricing logic. Clarification was provided on how Allmoxy handles deleted attributes and their permanent reservation. Decisions Made Use Meta attributes for labor assignment across product categories. Price slab doors at $25/sq ft, painted MDF slab doors at $60/sq ft, and five-piece painted MDF doors at $75/sq ft. Set a fallback labor price of $40/door for doors under 1.5 sq ft. Casework labor rates: Base: $125/lineal ft Tall: $250/lineal ft Drawer box labor: Dovetail: $175 Standard: $20 Rollouts: $120 Glide cost will be included directly in pricing using existing tables since standard hardware is always used. Challenges or Concerns Evan requested further clarification and training on how attributes and pricing formulas function in Allmoxy. Awareness was raised about the irreversible nature of attribute names in Allmoxy and the cascading effects of deleting them. Marques noted uncertainty about integrating laminated five-piece door options, which remain under development. There’s some need for future enhancement around installation pricing visibility and material tracking (e.g., sheet usage). Action Items Carson to send the Zoom recording and transcript for reference. Evan to review the recording and begin hands-on input of materials, attributes, and pricing adjustments in Allmoxy. Marques to provide updated pricing numbers for painted MDF slabs and five-piece doors and help configure new product types. Aaron to finalize proxy formulas and push them to all relevant product types once meta attributes are assigned. Evan & Marques to attach and default meta attributes to all relevant cabinet products in the catalog. Next Steps Evan and Marques to independently input data and test pricing logic in Allmoxy. Once comfortable, they’ll reach out to Carson to schedule a follow-up session. Carson will coordinate availability with Aaron for the next review session, potentially the following week or last week of May depending on progress. The session served as an introduction to the team, including Marques' success manager (Carson), implementation engineer (Aaron), and advisor (Bobby), and outlined the scope of the implementation. Context: Marques recently completed a remodel and equipment installation in a 1,000+ sqft shop, acquiring key machines including a 5x10 CNC, a vertical CNC, and an Altendorf F5 edgebander. The team is transitioning to Allmoxy with initial setup focused on building a product catalog and integrating workflows with Cabinet Vision. Urgency: There is moderate urgency due to recent technical setbacks (a computer crash resulting in data loss), and a desire to operationalize the platform swiftly. Key Takeaways Important Discussions Equipment Setup: Shop is operational with full CNC capabilities and a new edgebander. Allmoxy Integration: Initial focus is on catalog setup, attribute configuration, and aligning Allmoxy's product logic with Cabinet Vision exports. Cabinet Vision Data Loss: Marques lost a week of product/pricing data due to BitLocker reset on a new computer—catch-up work is ongoing. Technical Issues & Fixes Data Chain Integrity: Aaron emphasized the importance of attribute linkage and formula integrity in Allmoxy (highlighted by pink boxes for missing references). Cabinet Vision Integration: ORD file generation from Allmoxy will transfer data to Cabinet Vision, but formula/pricing setup must be duplicated in both systems manually. Export Mapping: Precise export names from Cabinet Vision must match Allmoxy’s export fields exactly to avoid breakdowns. Decisions Made Marques will: Begin defining dropdown menus for attributes (materials, drawer types, toe kicks, etc.). Limit door offerings initially to slab doors, delaying MDF and 5-piece options until pricing and CNC setup are finalized. Create construction methods in Cabinet Vision specifically for Allmoxy compatibility. Aaron and Carson will assist with formula creation and platform orientation. Challenges or Concerns Marques needs time to familiarize himself with Allmoxy and finalize product/pricing strategy. Training Evan (partner) and catching up on lost Cabinet Vision work adds pressure. Concerns about system complexity; emphasis on avoiding over-engineering.
