Title: Allmoxy Kick Off Call Date: Thu Apr 24 2025 11:00:00 GMT-0400 (Eastern Daylight Time) Participants: aaron@allmoxy.com, bobby@allmoxy.com, carson@allmoxy.com, marques@subtlecabinets.com Transcript: See full transcript Audio: Listen to audio Duration: 68 mins Overview The Allmoxy Kick Off Call was an introductory meeting between the Allmoxy team and Marques from Subtle Cabinets, focusing on the implementation of the Allmoxy software following a recent shop remodel. Key topics included an overview of the Allmoxy interface, system functionalities, and the integration with Cabinet Vision, with emphasis on establishing proper naming conventions for data transfer. The discussion highlighted the importance of setting up product attributes and dropdown options, with guidance on starting with slab door configurations. Action items for Marques involved dedicating time to explore the Allmoxy system, identifying pricing structures, and creating a specific construction method in Cabinet Vision. The meeting concluded with scheduling a follow-up for further discussions, underscoring the team's commitment to a collaborative and structured implementation process. Notes 🚀 Introduction and Background Setup Meeting introduced Bobby, Carson (success rep), and Aaron (implementation engineer) to Marques from Subtle Cabinets. Marques has recently completed shop remodel with CNC machine, vertical CNC, and Altendorf F5 Edge Bander. Marques explained his partner couldn't join due to illness. Shop is approximately 1,000 square feet with capability for 1 mil and half mil edge banding. Marques mentioned experiencing a computer crash that resulted in lost Cabinet Vision data. Discussion established that Marques has already imported and tested the template in Cabinet Vision. 📋 System Functionality Overview Aaron demonstrated Allmoxy interface including orders page and settings panel. Explained the 'pink boxes' error indicators that help identify missing data. Covered product page functionality including attributes, pricing, and parts tabs. Discussed formulas and how they work within Allmoxy system. Showed how attributes must be attached to products before they can be referenced in formulas. Explained how proxy variables work to enable global changes across products. Demonstrated testing sections for formulas to verify calculations without affecting total price. 🔧 Cabinet Vision Integration Discussed how Allmoxy exports data to Cabinet Vision through export codes. Clarified that Marques needs to manually enter pricing in Allmoxy, not import from Cabinet Vision. Bobby explained Marques would need to set up construction methods in both Cabinet Vision and Allmoxy. Confirmed that Allmoxy will create an ORD file that can be imported into Cabinet Vision. Established naming conventions between systems must match for proper data transfer. Discussed that Marques should focus on making a specific construction method in Cabinet Vision for Allmoxy. 📊 Product Configuration Focused on setting up dropdown menus for product attributes. Discussed adding different construction types like leg levelers and separate toe kicks. Aaron showed how to make attributes visible or hidden across products. Bobby recommended starting with defining what options should be available in dropdowns. Discussed image configurations for product visualization. Established that Marques wants to start with slab doors before adding more complex door types. 📈 Next Steps and Implementation Approach Carson emphasized the complexity of the system and reassured Marques this is normal. Bobby recommended focusing on defining dropdowns and pricing structure first. Aaron emphasized the system's flexibility and recommended keeping implementation straightforward. Discussed the importance of making the system transferable to other staff in the future. Carson suggested identifying the most complex cabinet type to define maximum required attributes. Bobby suggested pulling data from Cabinet Vision for initial configuration when possible. Onboarding #2 with Rigel Team 12/30/24 Tags These are ways you can group customers together for a certain purpose Cabinet dealers and contractors Pricing based on number of units over a 6 month time period Bronze, silver, gold, platinum (discount off retail price) These can be referenced in triggers and price adjustments Ex. you have a group of customers that are cabinet shops, and they get a certain discount. You can give this group of customers a "cabinet shop" tag on their company profile that can then be referenced later. You can also put tags on products How do you think you might group certain customers together? Price Adjustments Do you have customers that are priced differently than others? Why? Use price adjustments to achieve this Retail vs Wholesale Say you have a customer that is your oldest and most loyal customer, you always give them a 10% discount no matter what. Price adjustments are basically discounts or surcharges that can be applied to customers, groups of customers, or products. They are adjusted PER ITEM, not the total order amount Priority For when there are multiple price adjustments competing with one another If one discount has a higher priority than the other, the highest priority will override the other discount Ex. if you have a new customer discount and a summer sale discount going on at the same time, you would want the new customer discount to have a higher priority Tip: Use the Always setting, so you know if you are discounting or surcharging every time. You can also discount customers or products with certain tags Triggers How are you currently interacting with customers? Everything is manual (phone and emails) Triggers can automate that process for you Notify you, and your customers of something happening in Allmoxy Triggers to edit: 1, 6, 12, 16, 18, 19 Does he want to be notified of a bid? Title: Allmoxy Kick Off Call Date: Wed Dec 03 2025 16:45:00 GMT-0500 (Eastern Standard Time) Participants: bobby@allmoxy.com, joshb@allmoxy.com, carson@allmoxy.com, thinus@laneind.com.au Transcript: See full transcript Audio: Listen to audio Duration: 59 mins Overview - Product Catalog Setup: Focus on integrating a catalog of 50 product units using existing Cabinet Vision files for efficiency. - Pricing Structure: Fixed pricing based on unit size and minor adjustments, with variations like wedge inserts for curved walls. - Hybrid Build Approach: Almoxy’s engineer will initially build products, transferring responsibilities to the client as confidence grows. - Training Timeline: Initial training covers system basics before engineering work, with first build session scheduled for next week. - Strategic Vision: Automating drafting and order processes via Almoxy is key to improving speed and reducing manual work at OTR. - Operational Focus: Almoxy will ensure accurate data flow to Cabinet Vision, with attention to component details and minor dimension adjustments. Notes 👥 Meeting Introduction and Participant Introductions Focus on onboarding new Lane Industries team (Thinus, Dylan, David) to Almoxy. Carson Ward introduced as Customer Success Rep and Bobby Lewis as host. 📦 Discussion of Lane Industries’ Product Context Working with shopping centers and supermarkets. Challenges in syncing Jobman with MYOB and cloud limitations. 📋 Product Catalog Specifics OTR point-of-sale counters with proprietary designs. ~50 unit types with variations in dimensions; minimal price variation. Materials include 18mm plywood and MDF; special parts like stainless steel worktops. 🔧 Product Customization and Integration Discussion Need to automate order entries and product modifications into Cabinet Vision. Handling unit variations (width/length) and pricing models. Use of Almoxy portal for order placement by internal staff and resellers. 🗂️ Plans for Product Data Preparation Request to prepare a spreadsheet with products and allowed modifications. Encouragement for Lane staff to explore Almoxy system during the week. 📦 Clarification of Order Batching Capabilities Multiple store orders can be imported into one Cabinet Vision job for optimized nesting. ✅ Closing Remarks Affirming support and contact points (Bobby, Carson). Title: Allmoxy Scope Call - Date: Tue Nov 11 2025 18:00:00 GMT-0500 (Eastern Standard Time) Participants: bobby@allmoxy.com, thinus@laneind.com.au Transcript: See full transcript Audio: Listen to audio Duration: 56 mins Overview - Product Catalog Setup: Almoxy replicating Lean Industries’ 40-50 cabinetry items for better order processing with customizable attributes. - Cost for Catalog Build: Estimated engineering fees for catalog setup range between $2,000 and $4,000 due to complexity. - Workflow Automation: Almoxy automates order processing, linking customer orders directly to Cabinet Vision and shop machinery. - User Access Roles: Portal differentiates user roles for owners, employees, and customers, streamlining order entry and management. - Pricing Model: Initial focus on OTR product line with real-time price calculations and plans to expand pricing features later. - Trial and Implementation: Requested a trial run; agreed on a minimum contract of $250/month for six OTR cabinets build evaluation. Notes 👋 Meeting Commencement Connectivity checks and greetings were conducted. Bobby Lewis joined from a trade show in Canada; others were in Australia experiencing summer conditions. 🏢 Lean Industries Overview Lean Industries primarily focuses on retail joinery. They have a contract with a Shell Australia-affiliated field company requiring joinery work. There is a large potential in the Australian market size. 📂 Product Files Discussion Lean Industries uses Cabinet Vision PKG files. Bobby initially had trouble opening these files. Screen sharing was utilized to review the Cabinet Vision interface, jobs, and catalogs. 💾 Job and Catalog Saving Practices Jobs and catalogs are saved separately in Cabinet Vision. Saved jobs are preferred to ensure material setups remain consistent and reduce errors. 📊 Job Workflow Overview Typical job workflow includes approximately 40-50 standardized cabinets. Size variations depend on store layouts and specific units for larger or smaller stores. Focus is on repeatable units rather than fully custom layouts. 🖥️ Almoxy Software Portal Demonstration Bobby demonstrated Almoxy software portal capabilities. Product catalogs can be built with configurable variables, dropdowns, and dimension inputs. Pricing and order minimum/maximums can be user-set; exports to Cabinet Vision for CNC nesting are automated. 👥 User Roles in the Portal Discussion on internal sales/project managers vs external customers. Flexibility of order entry by clients or internal sales teams is important for efficiency. 🔄 Lean Industries Future Plans Plans to expand portal users to project managers, builders, shop fitters, and resellers with different trade terms. Their ERP Jobman manages pricing and accounting. ⚙️ Order Workflow Automation Almoxy automates order workflow from customer to verification, inventory allocation, and order document generation. Direct import into Cabinet Vision for production nesting is included, along with work schedule integration and finance links. 📐 Handling Drawings and Design Files Bobby cannot open certain drawings and design files due to software limitations on Mac. Possibility to attach files for manual workflows within Almoxy to track custom orders was discussed. 📦 Catalog Import and Product Matching Almoxy works product-based; images from Cabinet Vision can be used. Collaborative build of catalog by Almoxy engineer and Lean team is needed to ensure product attributes match. 🛠️ Catalog Customization Customization includes selectable construction methods with pricing formulas linked to selections. Real-time pricing during order entry is enabled. 💰 Pricing Management Discussion Lean Industries currently manages pricing via Excel and Jobman ERP. OTR pricing is controlled by purchasing; materials and finishes are standardized with limited variations. 📅 Next Steps for Catalog Building Bobby outlined next steps for catalog building with Alfine engineer sessions. Expected engineering cost for initial catalog setup is roughly $2,000-$4,000. 📝 Trial Build Proposal Proposal for trial build of 3-4 OTR cabinets for proof of concept discussed. Agreement to send pricing matrix and subscription documents shortly. Action Items Bobby Lewis Review the six Cabinet Vision files previously sent by Lean Industries to assess compatibility and confirm they represent the OTR catalog to be built into Almoxy Coordinate with Almoxy engineering to begin hybrid build of product catalog by working with Lean team to build and customize products and drop-down menus Send Lean Industries the pricing matrix and subscription agreement documents for Almoxy software, including options for sandbox or minimum contract trial Schedule kickoff call involving customer success rep, Almoxy engineer, and Lean team to launch catalog build process after subscription signing Lean Industries Confirm which products from the six sent represent the full OTR catalog to be built and identify any product edits or changes required for Almoxy Prepare to collaborate closely with Almoxy engineer on product catalog build for knowledge transfer and long-term management Review upcoming pricing and subscription details from Almoxy and decide on proceeding with trial or subscription

Title: Larkul Date: Wed Jul 23 2025 11:30:00 GMT-0400 (Eastern Daylight Time) Participants: bobby@allmoxy.com, dambuger@gmail.com, joshb@allmoxy.com Transcript: See full transcript Audio: Listen to audio Duration: 43 mins Overview - Josh Baker introduced himself as the customer success manager for Larkul, highlighting the challenges of conference attendance down to 10,000 compared to the typical 20,000 participants. - Josh's role as a non-billable project manager was clarified, with implementation engineers Aaron and Ray available at $150/hour for backend support. - A hybrid implementation method emerged, wherein the customer manages 95% of the workload, with engineering support provided as necessary. - The current product catalog includes floating shelves, mantles, and kitchen hoods, while display cases have been removed from the scope based on recent discussions. - Pricing for products employs linear foot pricing predominantly, with square foot pricing applied specifically to mantles. - The initial implementation meeting is set for August 22nd at 1:00 PM, after the customer's scheduled bow hunting trip. - Integration with the customer’s Mosaic system necessitates a live meeting for field mapping and export testing to ensure accurate data handling. - QuickBooks integration remains under development, expected to complete in two months, with a Transaction Pro workaround already in place. - User management discussions covered customizable permission levels for employee accounts and clarified public ordering protocols for pricing visibility. - The focus on B2B catalog integration and the potential post-launch exploration of marketplace features was addressed, with a preference for prioritizing pricing and Stripe setup first. Title: Allmoxy Kick Off Call Date: Fri Dec 12 2025 16:15:00 GMT-0500 (Eastern Standard Time) Participants: bobby@allmoxy.com, joshb@allmoxy.com, crystalcabinetworks@hotmail.com Transcript: See full transcript Audio: Listen to audio Duration: 35 mins Overview - Implementation Start: Team will upload a structured product template to fast-track Almoxy setup. - Pricing Adjustments Needed: Current pricing model has gaps; accurate costs for materials and finishes are essential. - Payment Processing Choice: Client will use Authorize.net for payments, prioritizing security over convenience. - User Access Management: Multiple users will be added to Almoxy, ensuring appropriate roles and limited financial visibility. - Communication Plan: Written communication will supplement calls to address language barriers and ensure clarity. - Next Steps: Engineer to upload product template, with pricing details and Authorize.net setup needed by Monday. Notes 👤 Introduction of Josh Baker Josh Baker introduced as the Customer Success Manager for the client account and implementation process with Almoxy. 🔑 Login Credentials and Template Preferences Discussion on login credentials and access to product templates. Client interested in exploring the template catalog, preferring default clean slate templates over extensive customizations. 💰 Pricing Concerns Identified gaps in pricing formulas within the provided templates that need adjustments for accuracy based on client-specific costs. 📊 Product Catalog Focus Clarified that the product catalog display will focus on the sales and order entry system rather than manufacturing software (Cabinet Vision). 🌐 Website Usage Plans Client plans to use the website primarily for product display rather than direct ordering, targeting local projects outside the website channel. ⚙️ Template Product Configuration Decision made for Almoxy engineer Aaron to push template products into the client’s instance and configure detailed pricing and dropdown options. 🛠️ Product Types Discussion Discussion on product types offered including doors, cabinets, and drawer boxes, with a commitment to incorporate accurate pricing. 💳 Payment Gateway Options Client prefers Authorize.net despite limitations; Almoxy to support Authorize.net setup. 📅 Active Invoices and Test Transactions Client has active invoices and work orders to process before year-end and wants to run test transactions. 🧾 Tax Rates and Shop Location Setup Setup of tax rates and default shop location for sales tax calculations discussed and partially configured. 👥 User Account Training Training on user account creation and permission assignment provided, indicating multiple users will be added. 📧 Next Steps Agreement Agreement to send client an email with a detailed list of pricing and product information needed for configuration. 🔄 Communication Challenges Concerns raised about communication challenges with the client, highlighting difficulties in understanding. ✉️ Need for Detailed Communication Acknowledgement that most communications may need to be handled via detailed emails or through other staff members. Action Items Bobby Lewis Coordinate with engineer Aaron to push the product templates into the client’s Almoxy instance Adjust payment gateway settings to use Authorize.net as preferred by client Send Dennis an email outlining all required product details and pricing information needed for configuration and implementation Josh Baker Guide Dennis through the implementation process and product catalog setup after templates are installed Assist in configuring financial settings, including tax presence and user permissions setup during the meeting and follow-ups Email client a detailed list requesting square foot pricing and product cost data to finalize pricing formulas Dennis Provide product cost data including pricing for doors, drawer boxes, finishes, and hardware to support template customization and proper pricing Obtain Authorize.net login credentials and transaction key from the payment processor team to enable payment gateway connection in Almoxy Set up user accounts and permissions for other team members who will access the Almoxy platform

Kick-off call with Bobby and Dennis 12/12/25 Intro Relationship between CS and implementation Build type (Hybrid/ Asynch)? Demo information Minnesota End customer: commercial builders and residential Product offering: framed and frameless cabinets Template catalog Cabinet Vision, QBO Resource allocation (eventually) REFERENCE MATERIAL

Title: Allmoxy Demo - : CRYSTAL CABINET WORKS Date: Wed Dec 03 2025 15:15:00 GMT-0500 (Eastern Standard Time) Participants: bobby@allmoxy.com, crystalcabinetworks@hotmail.com Transcript: See full transcript Audio: Listen to audio Duration: 42 mins Overview - Onboarding Ahead: Crystal Capital Works to start with $417/month subscription for expected $500,000 annual volume. - Setup Fee: Estimated setup fee of $5,000 to $10,000 for customization and integration. - Demo Instance: Custom demo instance and Cabinet Vision catalog will be provided for initial setup review. - Order Management: Software includes order management, inventory control, and customer self-service features. - Automated Communication: Automated email triggers will improve customer interactions and reduce manual follow-ups. - Timeline for Launch: System aimed to go live for order processing this winter after signing agreement. Notes 🔌 Video Connection Issues Discussed video connection issues at the start but proceeded without video successfully. 📦 Crystal Cabinet Works Overview Crystal Cabinet Works, based in Minnesota, seeks streamlined software for inventory, scheduling, invoicing, and order management, replacing Microsoft Business Electric 5 due to complexity. Company serves both commercial construction and private residential customers with framed and frameless cabinets, cabinet care and cleaning services, and operates a factory in Louisiana. 🖥️ Allmoxy Customer Portal Features Bobby Lewis explained Allmoxy’s customer portal allowing customers to view order status, outstanding balances, and make payments securely via Stripe integration supporting cards and ACH, emphasizing security and convenience. Discussed alternative payment gateway authorize.net for credit card payments but without stored cards; Stripe preferred for security and stored payment info. 📊 Integration with QuickBooks Online System integrates with QuickBooks Online for seamless syncing of invoices and payments, including automated past due reminders via email triggers. Product configurator allows building custom cabinetry orders with instant pricing; expert consultation needed to define product catalog and pricing. 💰 Tax and Pricing Management Software handles automatic tax calculation based on customer location/zipcode and allows manual override for tax-exempt customers. Supports pricing adjustments per customer or product with discounts or surcharges. Customers can specify shipping method with shipping costs automatically calculated and included in orders. 📋 Order Management Features Order management on owner side includes viewing bids, in-progress and completed jobs, inventory allocation and purchase order creation linked with inventory levels. Bobby Lewis confirmed ability to import Cabinet Vision catalogs into Allmoxy for streamlined integration with existing manufacturing software. 🛠️ Customization and Template Features Software allows template creation and supports customizable dropdown menus for product variations, including construction methods and door types. Partial payments and deposit requirements configurable with automated payment request emails containing payment links triggered by order status or customer tags. 📧 Automated Customer Communications Triggers automate customer communications including order confirmation, payment receipts, and shipping notifications to reduce phone calls. Supports itemized invoicing for services like cabinet cleaning and care, with customizable product attributes and photos. 🎨 Branding and Pricing Model Company logos and branding customizable in the software interface via theme uploads. Pricing model based on monthly subscription variable on annual sales volume; estimated $417/month for $500,000 annual volume with a 12-month minimum, plus a setup fee for engineering services ($5,000-$10,000 range) to build product catalog and customizations. 📝 Agreement Process and Next Steps Agreement process: contract to be sent upon meeting end; instance setup and catalog import initiated on contract signature; demo credentials and access to software to be provided for team review. Client emphasized urgency to implement and ability to make quick payment upon receiving contract; expressed strong positive impression of software ease of use and potential for business growth. Action Items Bobby Lewis Send subscription agreement for $417/month based on $500,000 annual volume Provide demo access with sample login credentials for review Import Cabinet Vision catalog matching Crystal Cabinet Works' products into Allmoxy instance Assist in defining dropdown options and pricing customization after initial setup Guide and support team during software onboarding and setup process AA / Crystal Cabinet Works Review Allmoxy demo and template catalog provided Sign subscription agreement promptly to initiate setup and contract process Coordinate internal team to evaluate software features and product catalog fit Make payment upon receipt of contract to expedite implementation Reach out via email with any further questions during setup phase

Catalog/retail-experience work happened March 19. Then the April 16 follow-up call failed entirely due to persistent audio issues -- the team switched to Zoom but no evidence the agenda was ever actually covered. Nothing since. Last Touchpoint April 16, 2026 -- Call (attempted) -- Sarah Pierce with Roland -- Technical/audio failures prevented any productive discussion; team agreed to switch platforms to Zoom going forward, but no follow-up call found since. Last Action Item Owner: Allmoxy (Sarah Pierce). Reschedule and actually hold the working session that April 16 failed to deliver. No evidence this happened in the 2.5 months since. Use Case & Launch Readiness Quick Kitchens CA (Roland) is setting up a B2B reseller storefront for Diamond CNC's cabinetry products, aiming to nest categories for commercial bids (mentioned a $200k cabinet job) and simplify retail options (5-6 colors) to reduce abandonment. Early-stage -- catalog structuring was still in progress when contact stopped. Sources Checked HubSpot (6 notes, including a formal handoff report from Bobby Lewis (sales) to Madison in mid-March -- ownership context worth noting), Fireflies (confirms no calls since the failed April 16 session), Gmail/Jira not separately checked given the small, clear picture already found. Flag: This is a fresh implementation that stalled on a literal technical failure (bad audio) rather than a real disagreement or blocker -- likely just needs to be rescheduled. Low risk, but easy to lose momentum on a new account if not picked back up soon.

Meeting with Sarah Pierce March 19, 2026 1:00 PM MDT 30 mins rolandsells@gmail.com sarah@allmoxy.com roland@quickkitchens.ca View Meeting Recording Product Catalog Structuring: Nesting categories for commercial clients will aid Roland in bidding for a $200,000 cabinet job. Retail Experience Simplification: Reducing options for retail clients to 5-6 colors aims to prevent order abandonment and confusion. Retail Site Launch Timeline: Targeting April 1st for a phased launch that will take several months to develop. Automated Payment Integration: Customers can pay online directly to Roland’s bank, streamlining order processing and minimizing manual management. Customization and Guidance: Branding adjustments require image resizing; detailed tutorials for retail clients will be developed by Roland. Sales and Partnership Strategy: Roland will focus on reselling without manufacturing, planning to invest sales revenue back into the platform's development. Product Catalog Structuring The focus is on organizing the product categories to improve commercial client bidding and prepare for retail sales. Folder and Category Setup for Commercial Use was prioritized to help Roland bid on a $200,000 cabinet job effectively (06:35) Sarah is creating nested categories reflecting Diamond CNC’s structure, including doors, full cabinet lines, hardware, accessories, and drawer boxes. This cleanup will replicate Diamond CNC’s organization to streamline ordering for knowledgeable commercial clients. Roland emphasized the urgency of this task to focus on bidding and commercial order placement. Sarah committed to finishing this within about 30 minutes and notifying Roland upon completion. Separation and Visibility of Multiple Catalogs for different cabinetry manufacturers was discussed to maintain clarity (25:39) Roland wants to keep other manufacturers’ catalogs separate and hidden unless authorized. Sarah explored tagging and catalog exclusivity but found no current system feature to hide B2B catalogs from each other. Roland will explore contacting manufacturers directly to manage orders and quotes independently. This reflects the complexity of handling multi-vendor inventory within Almoxy. Retail Customer Experience Simplification A strategic shift is needed to simplify the product offering for retail clients to enable self-service online ordering. Reducing Product Options for Retail Clients to avoid overwhelming customers and enable more straightforward online sales was identified as critical (07:50) Roland wants to limit choices to about 5-6 colors and fewer design lines compared to Diamond CNC’s extensive options. This simplification aims to prevent customer frustration and reduce order abandonment on the retail-facing site. Sarah highlighted that controlling option visibility is somewhat possible via filtering features but is limited by Diamond CNC’s catalog structure. Full custom catalogs for end consumers would require significant engineering effort and cannot be done quickly. Timeline for Retail Site Launch is targeted for April 1st, with a realistic expectation of a multi-month development process (09:14) Roland acknowledges that launching a customer-friendly retail platform will take several months of work. He plans to start with a simpler version and improve the system over time, similar to iterative product releases. Sarah confirmed the complexity and advised that building a full end-user catalog would exceed a two-week timeframe. This phased approach balances go-to-market speed with future platform enhancements. Order Processing and Payment Integration The system supports self-service ordering and secure payments directly to Roland’s bank account. Automated Payment Handling is integrated with Almoxy’s system to allow customers to pay via Visa or other methods online (18:24) Roland confirmed that payments go directly to his bank, simplifying order processing. Sarah validated that customers can create accounts, design kitchens, and place orders autonomously. This setup supports Roland’s goal of minimizing manual order management. It aligns with his desire to focus on sales rather than production or order handling. Customization and Branding Features Branding customization and user interface adjustments are available but require some image resizing and configuration. Site Logo and Side Image Placement were reviewed with Sarah showing how images appear on login and main pages (20:49) Roland uploaded logos and images but did not immediately see them on the site due to typical placement on the login page. Sarah explained image size requirements (1200x1800 pixels) and how header customization works. Roland considered removing the side image due to its current color scheme. This customization helps align the platform visually with Roland’s brand identity. Tutorials and User Guidance are partly supported through tooltips but require additional effort for detailed retail customer education (15:21) Almoxy uses Appcues for system-wide tooltips, but product-specific explainers must be added by catalog owners, like Mike. Roland plans to create his own video tutorials and educational content based on his cabinet-making expertise. This approach will help retail customers navigate complex options and reduce confusion. It also complements the simplified product offering to improve user experience. Strategic Sales and Partnership Approach Roland aims to leverage existing relationships and focus on sales while respecting supplier constraints. Partnership with Diamond CNC remains central, with Roland acting as a reseller driving sales without manufacturing cabinets himself (12:29) He emphasized his preference to outsource cabinet production and concentrate on selling. Roland respects Mike’s established catalog and does not want to disrupt his business model. This dynamic shapes the scope of customization and product offering modifications. Roland’s sales focus drives the need for streamlined product visibility and easy ordering. Future Platform Development Budgeting will be incremental, starting with a functional site and reinvesting sales revenue into improvements (19:39) Roland plans to launch a basic version early, then allocate funds to enhance the sales platform based on generated revenue. This phased investment mirrors common product launch strategies. Sarah agreed this approach is practical given the current system capabilities and market needs. It balances cost control with the ambition to build a robust retail sales channel over time. (06:08) Obtain and update product images from Diamond CNC corresponding to the new folder setup. (20:15) Notify Roland via email when folder restructuring and updates are completed, expected within about 30 minutes from meeting end. (16:29) Review the updated category/folder structure once Sarah completes the cleanup and confirm if it meets bidding needs. (20:33) Investigate options to manage multiple cabinetry product catalogs separately or reach out directly to other manufacturers as needed to avoid catalog overlap. (25:24) Consider resizing and adjusting branding images (site logo, side image) based on guidance for proper visual presentation on Almoxy login and header screens. (20:40) Plan phased rollout of retail online sales platform targeting April 1 launch with the intent to improve functionality over time. Platform Customization Options: Roland can import products and build custom ones, focusing on initial product library learning. Technical Issues Identified: Misconfigured platform instance led to pulling incorrect data; reset planned for resolution. Support Commitment: Sarah will provide documentation and follow-up to ensure smooth onboarding and address technical issues. Quick Import Post-Fix: Once resolved, importing Diamond CNC's catalog will take about five minutes to enable selling. User Experience Challenges: Roland faced usability struggles with screen sharing and confusing data in the platform interface. B2B Sales Setup and Product Integration The meeting focused on onboarding Roland Donald Sells as a new reseller for Diamond CNC's products through a B2B platform. Roland’s Sales Role and Product Scope Confirmed (07:36) Roland is a new sales representative focusing on cabinet sales and spinning up a website for that. He plans to resell all of Diamond CNC’s products initially through the platform. Roland aims for an 18% margin, which translates to approximately a 26% markup on product costs. No formal pricing agreement yet exists with Mike from Diamond CNC, so pricing strategy is still flexible. Platform Capabilities and Customization Options Explained (10:52) Sarah clarified that as a reseller, Roland can import Diamond CNC’s product catalog but also add products from other suppliers or build custom products. Roland expressed interest in importing Diamond CNC’s product library first and learning the platform through hands-on experience. Building custom products will require additional learning and potential communication with Mike for ordering specifics. Technical Challenges Identified with Product Setup (11:50) Roland struggled with platform features like configuring inch-and-a-half gables and setting up company branding and logos. Sarah offered assistance and documentation to help him get started with branding and B2B settings. The team acknowledged that product configuration is complex, but internal engineers with cabinet-building expertise are available to assist with custom product frameworks. B2B Account and Pricing Tier Impact Highlighted (14:00) Bobby informed Roland that moving into custom product creation would change his subscription type and potentially increase costs based on volume tiers. Roland confirmed he does not plan to manufacture cabinets himself, only resell, which keeps his account in the B2B reseller tier. Technical Issues and Next Steps for Platform Access The session encountered technical issues with Roland’s platform instance pulling incorrect data, delaying product setup. Instance Misconfiguration Causing Data Pull Issues (16:00) Sarah discovered Roland was connected to a template/test environment instead of the correct production instance. This caused the system to pull non-customer test data instead of Diamond CNC’s actual supplier data. Bobby confirmed this was an internal setup issue on their side, not Roland’s fault. Reset and Reconfiguration Planned to Fix Instance (18:00) Sarah and Bobby planned to log out, reset Roland’s instance by cloning from an empty master template, and attempt to sync correctly. If the reset does not resolve the issue, developer intervention will be required, delaying setup beyond the meeting. Roland agreed to keep the call open and rejoin once the issue is fixed. Follow-Up Support and Scheduling Next Meeting (19:50) Sarah committed to reporting the issue to developers with a goal to fix it quickly. She will follow up by email with documentation on branding and company setup to prepare Roland in the meantime. A follow-up meeting will be scheduled, ideally for the next morning, to complete product import and setup once the instance is fixed. Quick Product Catalog Import Expected After Fix (20:20) Bobby highlighted that once the instance issue is resolved, importing Diamond CNC’s catalog will take about five minutes. This step will enable Roland to start selling products promptly after technical issues are cleared. Customer Success and Support Strategy The discussion emphasized hands-on support and gradual onboarding to ensure Roland can independently manage the platform. Sarah’s Role as Customer Success Lead and Support Resource (08:19) Sarah positioned herself as the main contact for guiding Roland through the B2B structure and onboarding process. She reassured Roland that the team would assist with complex product building and customization. Learning-by-Doing Approach Encouraged (11:20) Roland prefers learning the platform through trial and error, supported by documentation and expert help. Sarah agreed this approach fits well with the available training materials and on-demand engineering support. Documentation and Training Materials to Be Provided (13:30) Sarah will send Roland materials covering branding setup, contact management, and product configuration basics. This will allow Roland to progress independently while waiting for the technical issue to be resolved. Engineering Support for Complex Product Builds (12:20) The team’s engineers have several years of cabinet-building experience and can accelerate custom catalog creation. This resource is available if Roland decides to expand beyond standard product import. Platform Usability and User Experience Challenges The session revealed some usability hurdles that Roland faced with the software interface and screen sharing. Screen Sharing Technical Difficulties Slowed Progress (13:50) Roland initially struggled to share his screen, causing delays in live walkthroughs. Sarah and Bobby provided step-by-step guidance to enable screen sharing successfully. User Interface Confusion Around B2B Settings (15:58) Sarah directed Roland to locate the B2B settings gear icon to access supplier logos and product options. Despite this, the platform showed unexpected template data, causing confusion. Instance Environment Confusion Impacted User Confidence (16:30) Seeing test environment data instead of live production information created uncertainty for Roland. Clear communication from Sarah and Bobby helped maintain trust and set expectations for resolution. Recognition of Need for Improved Instance Management (19:00) The team acknowledged that instance cloning and environment setup could be streamlined to avoid such issues. Bobby expressed openness to adjusting processes if current methods prove unreliable. Action Items Roland Donald Log out and assist with resetting the Allmoxy instance as directed. (18:42) Sarah Pierce Reset Roland’s instance by cloning from the master empty template for accurate product and supplier data. (19:05) Report technical issues to the developers to fix the environment so Diamond CNC products appear correctly. (19:55) Send Roland documentation on setting up companies, contacts, and branding while waiting for issue resolution. (20:25) Schedule a follow-up call after developer fixes, aiming for the next day. (20:25) Bobby Lewis Provide Sarah with the pricing matrix for volume tier subscription changes related to custom product manufacturing. (14:00) Meeting Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/view/01KKSVF21QE57SE3PSFD607XSG 📎 Time markers in this document can be used to navigate to specific points in the meeting recording Processed by:

Quick Kitchens CA Handoff Report from Head of Sales to Madison 1. Account Snapshot Company: Quick Kitchens CA (quickkitchens.ca Ltd.) HubSpot Company ID: 52560026544 Website / Domain: quickktchens.ca (typo in record; brand is “Quick Kitchens CA”) Allmoxy Instance: https://quickkitchens.allmoxy.com (B2B portal for Roland) Lifecycle Stage: Customer Owner (to date): Bobby Lewis – Head of Sales Associated deals: 1 (customer total revenue recorded: $200 so far) Associated contacts: 1 primary contact (Roland; details below) Last sales activity: 2026‑03‑04 Last logged contact & note: 2026‑03‑14 (Instance‑ready email + kickoff plan) From my perspective, this is a very new, high‑potential B2B reseller account that has just converted from evaluation to paid and is entering onboarding. The relationship is positive and engaged, but execution and time‑to‑value will depend heavily on how smoothly you (Madison) run onboarding and coordinate with Mike’s supplier catalog side. 2. Key Contacts & Roles Primary Contact Name: Roland (full name in contact record; primary stakeholder) Email: rolandsells@gmail.com Role: Owner of Quick Kitchens CA’s new online cabinetry channel Also acts as a sales rep for Mike’s commercial accounts (dual role: reseller + rep) Context: Small team (form data: 1–5 employees, $1.5M–$4.5M annual revenue) Already familiar with Allmoxy through existing user (form: “What brings you to Allmoxy? – Allmoxy User (A company that's already using allmoxy)”). He’s not coming in cold; expectations are relatively high because he’s seen Allmoxy in action elsewhere. Very hands‑on, entrepreneurial, and comfortable with tooling (willing to own website/landing page creation and portal configuration with guidance). Other Stakeholders Mike(Diamond CNC). Not a stakeholder (not in our CRM as a contact for this company, but central to the model): Owns the source catalog that Roland will resell. Our system pulls products, pricing, and options from Mike’s Allmoxy instance to Roland’s. Needs to approve Roland as a reseller in his instance, and his shipping/pricing structures are the base for Roland’s margin. For your work, Roland is the operational owner you’ll work with day‑to‑day. Mike is an external dependency we coordinate around for catalog and shipping logic. 3. Relationship & Interaction History (Chronological Overview) 3.1 Discovery & Demo (Early March 2026) 2026‑03‑05 – Allmoxy Demo (Zoom meeting) Meeting: “Allmoxy Demo – : quickkitchens.ca Ltd.” (35 minutes, recorded via Fireflies). Participants: me (Bobby), Roland. Focus: Designing a B2B online sales platform where Roland resells Mike’s cabinetry catalog under the Quick Kitchens brand. Key outcomes from the demo (from my meeting note): Business Model & Catalog Setup Roland will resell cabinetry products online using Mike’s catalog, not maintain his own from scratch. Customers visit a Quick Kitchens branded portal and order products; orders flow automatically into Mike’s system. This eliminates double entry and lets Roland go to market quickly. Customer Journey End customers (mostly homeowners) create accounts before ordering. They upload existing cabinet drawings; Roland is not offering drawing or design services. System supports: Single or multiple item orders Optional credit limits and B2B terms (if he wants to expand beyond homeowners later). Roland can limit which products/options are visible on his instance to keep the catalog simple for end customers. Payments & Cash Flow Payments handled via integrated Stripe: Credit cards and bank transfers (similar to Canadian e‑transfers). Processing fee: 2.9% per credit card transaction. Funds go directly to Roland’s bank account. Offline payments like checks are supported as manual options. Shipping & Fulfillment Mike ships directly to Roland’s customers. Shipping costs will be calculated via configurable B2B shipping formulas, based on Mike’s rates plus Roland’s markup. We stressed that shipping cost logic must be aligned with Mike’s team to avoid margin surprises. Website / Front‑End Experience The Allmoxy side provides the portal (quickkitchens.allmoxy.com) — effectively the “storefront back end”. We recommended a simple landing page to: Explain the Quick Kitchens brand and offer. Warm customers before they enter the ordering experience. I showed Roland the Lovable AI website builder as a low‑cost, fast way to spin up a landing page: Uses his logos/brand colors. Can include a prominent “Order Online” button linking to the Allmoxy portal. ~$20 cost, he can manage it himself. Subscription & Instance Subscription fee: $199 USD / month. Upon signing, we: Create a custom instance for Quick Kitchens. Connect to Mike’s product catalog and apply Roland’s markup. A customer success representative (you/CS) will: Guide him through catalog connection. Help set pricing and shipping formulas. Train him on day‑to‑day use. Strategic Value Roland avoids building a catalog from scratch; time‑to‑market is short. This is one of the simplest, highest‑return setups we see: supplier already on Allmoxy, reseller running a lean online sales operation. Roland also keeps his role as rep for Mike’s commercial accounts, so this system complements his existing activity instead of replacing it. Meeting Action Items (from the note) For Roland: Set up hosting & build a landing page using AI builder or equivalent. Review and sign the subscription agreement I sent. Confirm markup structure over Mike’s base pricing. For Allmoxy (Bobby → CS team): Send subscription agreement and documentation. After agreement: Create the Quick Kitchens instance. Integrate Mike’s product catalog as a reseller feed. Assign a customer success rep (you) to lead onboarding. Support Roland with domain DNS and linking: His quickktchens.ca domain pointing to landing page + portal. Most of these are now in motion (see next section). 3.2 Conversion & Early Onboarding (Mid March 2026) Subscription & Instance Creation Email – “Sign Up” (2026‑03‑12) I emailed Roland confirming receipt of the signed subscription agreement. Key content: I acknowledged the agreement coming through and explained that putting a card on file triggers instance creation and internal processes. I nudged him to revisit the document link he signed to complete payment details and finalize setup. Tone: excited, supportive, and focused on getting to instance creation quickly. Email – “Instance Ready” (2026‑03‑14) This is the critical onboarding transition: I confirmed that we created his instance and are configuring it based on previous conversations. Shared portal login: URL: https://quickkitchens.allmoxy.com/public/login/ Username: rolandsells@gmail.com Temporary password: password123 (asked him to change immediately in his profile). I told him we’re ready for a kickoff call with Customer Success (you & Sarah) and gave him a meeting link to book: Suggested he invite anyone he wants involved, especially the main project point‑person. I set expectations that we’d create a specific plan to get his instance ready to introduce to his customers. At this point, in CRM: Company lifecycle is set to Customer. Total revenue shows $200 (likely initial charge; the main opportunity is in future B2B transaction volume). There is one associated deal and no open deals (hs_num_open_deals = 0), indicating initial sale is closed and we’re moving into adoption/expansion. 4. Product & Implementation Scope 4.1 Current Scope Product: Allmoxy B2B online ordering portal, reseller model. Instance: quickkitchens.allmoxy.com Initial configuration focus: Connect to Mike’s existing catalog. Implement Roland’s markup over Mike’s base pricing. Set visibility rules so Roland exposes only the subset of products/options appropriate for his end customers. Configure Stripe with Roland’s banking details. Define shipping formulas consistent with Mike’s policies and Roland’s margins. 4.2 Planned Customer Experience Prospective customer hits Roland’s landing page (non‑Allmoxy front‑end he will create). They click “Order Online” or similar CTA and are taken to the Allmoxy portal. They create an account and upload drawings. Orders flow to Roland’s Allmoxy instance → then replicate into Mike’s system after Roland’s verification. Payments are captured via Stripe (or recorded offline for checks). Mike ships directly to the end customer. Your onboarding work should make this flow feel cohesive and low‑friction. 5. Commercials & Business Potential Subscription: $199 USD/month (standard for this configuration). Recorded revenue so far: $200 (likely initial billing). Deal count: 1 closed/won; no other open deals. Upside: The value here is not in subscription ARPU alone but in: Volume of cabinetry through the portal. Roland’s ability to scale quickly without adding headcount. If onboarding goes well, there is: Potential to expand catalog coverage. Introduce B2B account features (credit terms, more complex pricing). Eventually add services or additional Allmoxy modules as his operation grows. 6. Sentiment, Risks, and Opportunities 6.1 Sentiment From all interactions and recorded notes: Roland is excited and optimistic: He reacted positively to seeing how fast we can spin up a reseller instance. He liked the idea that most heavy lifting (catalog, pricing) is already done on Mike’s side. No negative sentiment logged; no tickets or escalations yet. Tone from my emails is intentionally encouraging: “We are really excited to work with you… Thank you again for trusting us. Let’s get going!!” While that’s my wording, Roland’s engagement (signing quickly, moving into setup) confirms he is motivated to move fast. 6.2 Key Risks Landing Page & Domain Stall Roland needs to: Choose/confirm a hosting approach. Build or publish the landing page. Configure quickktchens.ca DNS correctly. If this drags, the portal exists but has no traffic, and enthusiasm may fade. Shipping & Pricing Misalignment Shipping formulas require coordination with Mike: If shipping costs are misestimated, Roland’s margins can be wiped out, or customers see unexpected delivery charges. Similarly, if markup is not carefully thought through, he could be uncompetitive or unprofitable. Roland’s Bandwidth He’s a small team (1–5 people) plus rep duties for Mike. If onboarding feels heavy or confusing, he may delay configuration work and underutilize the system. Expectation Management (Existing Allmoxy Exposure) Because he’s already seen Allmoxy in another company, he may expect: High polish from day one. Very quick ROI. If we don’t deliver a “quick win,” sentiment could flip. 6.3 Opportunities Fast Time‑to‑Value Catalog already exists; we’re not starting from zero. If you move quickly with him on: Stripe Shipping formulas Basic page content He can realistically start taking online orders very soon. Case Study Material If this succeeds, it’s an ideal case study: Allmoxy user → layered reseller model → new revenue stream, minimal overhead. We could later showcase this to other shops with similar supplier relationships. Expansion Over time: Advanced B2B features (credit, purchase order workflows). Possible multi‑catalog setup (Roland reselling products from multiple suppliers). Adding internal production management if he ever starts fabricating in‑house. 7. Recommended Next Steps for Madison Here’s what I recommend you focus on in your first 30–45 days as the new owner of this account. 7.1 Immediate (Next 1–2 Weeks) Kickoff Call Use the meeting link I provided in the “Instance Ready” email (or send a fresh invite if he hasn’t booked). Objectives: Align on go‑live target date. Confirm roles (who else, if anyone, will help him internally). Re‑confirm the customer journey in his own words: How he wants customers to find the site. What he wants them to do before they place an order. Discuss success criteria: e.g., “X orders/month by [date]” or “first paying order within Y weeks.” Checklist Review with Roland Walk through a lightweight launch checklist, including: Stripe account connection. DNS and domain pointing (quickktchens.ca → landing page + portal link). User roles (who besides Roland needs admin access). Basic email templates / branding in the portal. Make everything feel concrete and finite, not overwhelming. Instance Health Check Confirm: Quick Kitchens instance is accessible and branded correctly. Roland’s login works and password has been changed. Mike’s catalog integration status (if already wired up by Services/CS, just validate with Roland). 7.2 Short‑Term (Weeks 2–4) Shipping & Pricing Workshop Facilitate a working session to: Review Mike’s shipping rules. Implement B2B shipping formulas in Roland’s instance. Validate that he understands how price → markup → margin works. Where needed, coordinate a joint call with Mike’s team to avoid assumptions. Portal Walkthrough & Training Focus on: Approving & managing incoming orders. Handling payments (Stripe capture, refunds, manual payments). Managing customers (accounts, credit limits if he uses them). Basic reporting so he can see how his channel is performing. Launch Milestone Aim to reach a clear milestone like: “First real customer order placed end‑to‑end through the portal.” Celebrate that with him; it’s a psychological anchor that Allmoxy is “live” and working. 7.3 Medium‑Term (Post‑launch, 1–3 Months) Performance Review Once he has order volume: Review order data, average order size, payment behavior. Explore tweaks to markup, promotions, or shipping to improve conversion. Opportunities for Expansion Based on his results: Offer to help him add: New product lines from Mike. Additional suppliers. More sophisticated B2B features. Discuss whether he wants to use more Allmoxy features beyond the reseller front end. 8. What You Should Watch Closely Is Roland progressing on his landing page and domain? If not, consider giving him: Example content. A pre‑built copy deck. Clear “good enough” standards so he doesn’t overthink it. Has he actually logged into the instance and changed his password? Quick verification during kickoff will confirm if he has engaged. Are there any early frictions with Stripe or shipping formulas? These are the most likely blockers to going live; prioritize unblocking them. Is he still excited after the first month? If activity drops, re‑center the conversation on his original goal: build an online sales engine without building a full manufacturing operation. 9. Summary for You as New Owner Quick Kitchens CA is a fresh, high‑intent reseller customer built around a strong existing supplier (Mike) and a motivated operator (Roland). We have: A live instance (quickkitchens.allmoxy.com). A signed subscription and first revenue in the system. A clear, documented B2B storefront model. Positive momentum from our early interactions. Your success on this account will hinge on: Running a smooth, confidence‑building onboarding. Turning the portal from “configured” into “actively selling”. Helping Roland hit his first few live orders quickly so the value of Allmoxy is obvious. If you need deeper context, the Fireflies meeting recording and note linked in the company’s associated engagements provide a detailed play‑by‑play of the demo and expectations we set.

Allmoxy Demo - : quickkitchens.ca Ltd. March 5, 2026 3:45 PM MST 35 mins bobby@allmoxy.com rolandsells@gmail.com View Meeting Recording B2B Online Sales Platform Setup The meeting focused on enabling Roland to resell cabinetry products online using Mike's existing catalog through a B2B system with seamless order and payment integration. Launch of Reseller Online Store Using Mike’s Catalog (08:26) Roland plans to sell cabinetry products online by subscribing to Mike’s product catalog within Bobby’s system. Customers will browse and order products directly from Roland’s branded portal, which automatically syncs prices and options from Mike’s catalog. Orders verified by Roland are instantly created in Mike’s system, eliminating double entry and streamlining fulfillment. Bobby emphasized this setup requires minimal configuration since Mike maintains product data and pricing. Customer Journey and Account Creation Process (12:56) End customers, mostly homeowners, will create accounts on Roland’s portal before ordering. Customers upload existing cabinet drawings, as Roland will not provide drawing services. The system handles both single and multiple item orders, with options for credit limits and B2B terms if needed. Roland can limit product options shown to customers by configuring settings on his instance. Order Verification and Payment Integration (16:52) Roland receives orders in his portal and verifies them before submission to Mike’s system. Payments are collected through an integrated Stripe setup, supporting credit cards and bank transfers similar to Canadian e-transfers. Payment processing fees are 2.9% per credit card transaction, with funds deposited directly into Roland’s bank account. Offline payments like checks are also supported, providing flexibility for customers. Shipping and Fulfillment Coordination (20:21) Mike will ship products directly to Roland’s customers. Shipping costs will be calculated via configurable B2B shipping formulas based on Mike’s shipping rates plus any markup. Bobby highlighted the importance of coordinating shipping cost formulas with Mike’s team to ensure accuracy and profitability. Website and Landing Page Development Roland needs a landing page to present his brand and direct customers to the ordering system, with AI tools recommended for easy creation. Website Options and Domain Integration (22:27) Roland does not need a fully hosted website; the system can provide a branded portal at quickkitchens.allmoxy.com as a standalone store. However, a front-end landing page is recommended to explain services and build trust before customers order. This landing page can link directly to the ordering portal via an “Order Online” button. AI-Powered Website Builder Recommendation (24:19) Bobby demonstrated an AI tool called Lovable that quickly generates a professional landing page using provided logos and brand colors. The AI builder can add custom buttons linking to Roland’s ordering portal automatically. This tool costs about $20 and allows Roland to create and publish his landing page himself, saving development costs. Domain Setup and Hosting (29:17) Roland will need to configure his domain registrar (CanSpace) to point to the landing page and ordering portal. Bobby advised keeping hosting plans simple and basic since the system is lightweight. The team can start integrating catalogs and pricing while Roland works on the landing page. Subscription, Pricing, and Onboarding Process The system uses a subscription model with clear pricing, markup control, and a guided onboarding process involving key stakeholders. Subscription Cost and Setup (17:30) The monthly subscription fee for the system is $199 USD. Upon agreement signing and payment setup, Bobby’s team creates a custom instance for Roland (e.g., company.allmoxy.com). The instance syncs Mike’s selected products with Roland’s markup automatically applied. Markup Control and Product Approval (33:38) Roland determines his selling prices by adding a markup to Mike’s base prices. Mike must approve Roland as a reseller to allow product access in his system. A customer success representative guides Roland through the approval and setup process. Customer Success and Documentation Delivery (32:44) Bobby is sending the subscription agreement and documentation immediately to kickstart onboarding. A customer success agent will be assigned to assist with connecting to Mike’s catalog and training on system usage. Roland plans to finalize hosting today and start building his landing page to align with onboarding milestones. Strategic Business Impact and Growth Potential This integration aims to create a scalable online sales channel leveraging existing supplier infrastructure, reducing operational overhead for Roland. Streamlined Sales Channel with Minimal Catalog Maintenance (10:56) By leveraging Mike’s product catalog and pricing, Roland avoids the time-consuming task of building and maintaining a product database. This model allows quick deployment and faster time to revenue, critical for Roland’s business growth. Bobby described this approach as one of the easiest setups with a high potential return. Dual Role as Reseller and Sales Rep (10:17) Roland will act both as a reseller through the online portal and as a sales rep handling Mike’s commercial accounts. This dual approach increases sales opportunities and diversifies revenue streams. Leveraging the digital platform complements Roland’s existing rep work, broadening market reach. Competitive Advantage via Seamless Integration and Payment Flexibility (31:32) Integrated Stripe payments simplify customer transactions and fund flow, improving cash flow and user experience. Support for multiple payment types, including credit cards and bank transfers, meets diverse customer preferences. The ability to customize shipping and pricing formulas ensures Roland can remain competitive while protecting margins. Action Items Roland Donald Sells Set up hosting platform and start building a landing page using AI website builder or other means. (26:40) Review and sign subscription agreement sent by Bobby Lewis to initiate Allmoxy service setup. (32:49) Confirm markup pricing over Mike’s product costs for setting up sales pricing. (33:38) Bobby Lewis Send subscription agreement and documentation to Roland for review and signature. (32:49) Upon agreement, create B2B instance for Roland’s Quick Kitchens, integrate Mike’s product catalog, and assign a customer success representative to assist with onboarding. Title: Allmoxy Demo - The Premier Hub Date: Thu Apr 03 2025 17:15:00 GMT-0400 (Eastern Daylight Time) Participants: bobby@allmoxy.com, cheneil@allmoxy.com, juan@thepremierhub.com, nathalia@thepremierhub.com Transcript: See full transcript Audio: Listen to audio Duration: 64 mins Overview The Product Demo and Requirements Gathering meeting for The Premier Hub's integration with Allmoxy featured Juan and Natalia from The Premier Hub, alongside Bobby Lewis from Allmoxy, who demonstrated their online sales solution tailored for custom cabinetry. The meeting began with introductions and an overview of The Premier Hub’s business model, currently 70% B2C and 30% B2B, with plans to enhance B2B sales. Key to the discussion was the need for Allmoxy's system to integrate with their existing Mosaic setup while allowing for streamline operations as The Premier Hub prepares to franchise. Bobby showcased Allmoxy's capabilities, including real-time pricing and automatic generation of Mosaic files upon order placement. Despite initial pricing concerns, adjustments were made based on their current sales volume, and a plan for a custom catalog was discussed to ensure operational clarity. Action items were assigned, including sending demo links and catalog templates, as well as a follow-up meeting to explore material options, ensuring both teams are aligned for effective implementation. Notes 🏢 Introductions and Company Background Juan and Natalia from The Premier Hub, a custom cabinetry shop in South Florida Bobby Lewis from Allmoxy demonstrating their online sales solution Juan mentioned they've previously had a meeting with Allmoxy about a year ago Juan explained they're seeking an online sales solution similar to what Allmoxy provides for DOT Cabinets The Premier Hub currently uses Mosaic for cabinet design and manufacturing Juan noted business is currently 70% B2C and 30% B2B, with goal to increase B2B to 45% 🔄 Business Model and Integration Needs Juan explained they need a system that integrates with their existing Mosaic setup The Premier Hub is planning to franchise their business model and partner with a Colorado company Juan described how they compete with Chinese/prefab cabinets by offering American-made custom cabinets Bobby confirmed Allmoxy can integrate with Mosaic, sending data directly to it Juan explained they currently use DOT Cabinets' website to quickly price cabinets Bobby demonstrated how Allmoxy can provide real-time pricing for custom cabinet sizes 💰 Pricing Structure and Implementation Juan questioned how the Mosaic integration works with Allmoxy Bobby explained Allmoxy handles business operations, ordering, payments, and inventory management Bobby explained that Allmoxy can send cabinet specifications to Mosaic for manufacturing Monthly pricing discussed: $1,200/month for $2M annual sales volume Juan indicated this was higher than expected (they pay $382 for Mosaic licenses) Bobby adjusted pricing to $500-550/month based on current monthly sales of $100,000 🛠️ Implementation Details Bobby offered to provide a catalog template that matches with a Mosaic catalog Juan emphasized wanting to start small ('less is more') with limited options Juan wants fewer material options than DOT Cabinets offers to streamline operations Bobby confirmed they can create a custom catalog matching Juan's requirements The integration would allow orders placed online to generate Mosaic files automatically Bobby explained implementation would include formula creation for pricing calculations 📊 Catalog and Product Management Juan asked if Allmoxy needs access to their Mosaic database Bobby clarified he would just provide a product library file that matches Allmoxy's catalog Juan explained his vision for a physical inventory of pre-cut cabinet components to reduce delivery time Bobby agreed the business model is viable and Allmoxy is well-positioned to support it Natalia asked about adding hardware products to the catalog (trash bins, spice racks, etc.) Bobby demonstrated how they could add products and have full control over their catalog 🔗 Final Details and Next Steps Bobby explained The Premier Hub's domain would be tph.allmoxy.com The system would include payment processing via Stripe (2.9% fee) Juan asked about showing credit card fees as separate line items on invoices Bobby will send demo links for Juan and team to explore the platform Bobby mentioned QuickBooks Online integration is coming soon Juan stated his franchise partner may also want to implement Allmoxy for their prefab cabinet lines Action Items Bobby Lewis Send demo link for The Premier Hub team to explore the Allmoxy platform Create and share a Mosaic product catalog file that matches the Allmoxy catalog Send subscription agreement for monthly payment Send pricing matrix showing volume-based pricing tiers Set up a follow-up meeting to discuss material options and dropdowns Juan Review the demo and catalog with the team to confirm it contains what they need Create a list of desired door materials and options for the catalog Connect the franchise partner with Bobby to discuss implementation for their stores Send profit and loss statements from previous year to Bobby for pricing considerations

engagements.body: Regarding email: Innovative Cabinetry And Design​- Contract Saving Renewal, sent on Monday, August 5, 2024 11:21 AM

Renewal 2024 Things have been going well. Jed finally feels like he has the shop set up that he has worked out the bugs. Now he just needs more customers, plans on hiring someone for sales to help selling the software. I let him know that Carson would be available for training should he decide to have his sales person get super familiar with the Allmoxy system. The biggest allmoxy value add has been getting materials in but then they got busy and sidetracked with some side projects. They are having a hard time going all in on getting pricing correct because of the amount of changes that are happening post importing into cabinetvision. Whether it's the customers fault or whether that's just their flexibility, like they have a lot of flexibility on their end and are not forcing people into what they have to offer. They will pretty much do anything for their customers. So that is probably the main hang-up with going all in. Jed sees the value in clicking a few buttons and sending the invoice and whether its charging a credit card or whatever, because he spends about 4 hours a week at least or more billing on his end but its just all the custom stuff that he does on his end that he can't really just bill for straight out of the box with Allmoxy. He mentioned that even if it was just getting some sort of a custom product created where he could quickly edit the final price or whatever before he ships the products. He said and maybe that's the easiest way to do it because he feels like he is getting close, and has been paying attention to what prices it's been shooting out for most of the jobs and compared to how I'm billing it, and it's right there, plus or minus a percent or two of where he would like to be. But he feels like that's ok, it's just the custom materials it added or once we get it into Allmoxy and he transfers the ORDX, and he transfers the RDX into cabinet vision, then they make changes if they add a cabinet or two, because he usually sends them assembly sheets out of cabinet vision, and then it comes back to him with the changes before he tests it. By doing that, it changes the price and he just doesn't want to lose out on all the money. So he essentially needs a quick way to get into their order, update their price without updating the product, like a different product and trying to make it work or it's just something custom say the add one panel, but they want to be boarded or grooved or they want, like a flower design cut in or something like that. He just needs to quickly edit their order to what he wants it to be before he ships it. Additionally, it would be making sure that he understands the back and forth between that and Quickbooks since that would be a whole different ballgame. He is currently using Quickbooks desktop. He said there is a lot of his business that does not run through Allmoxy because of his own personal jobs or commercial side of things. So he needs it to all run in one financial software type. So he needs to be able to import those invoices or import those accounts receivable or something into Allmoxy or Quickbooks so he can keep track of it. He said the payment will probably still end up going through QuickBooks or obviously if it's credit card, it will go through Allmoxy. But somehow getting those payments imported into QuickBooks so he can keep everything in one tab would be big. The ORDX he thinks is figured out and he has most of the import of the materials done, he still has some to import, but most of the materials stuff is figured out. With pricing finally leveled off a little bit, he thinks the next step is just trying to speed up the invoicing process. He is attending IWF and arrives Tuesday. I let him know he could stop by the booth and talk with you in person @Carson Ward. Or if you miss each other you could link up after the show. Forgive me if these notes don't make sense. I did my best to keep notes and keep up. You can always watch the fireflies if that helps. Let me know if you have any questions. Thank you!
